videos.overview: Violence on Television since Hungerford massacre violence on television has become a hot political issue.

videos.title: The IRA: The Long War
videos.overview: A history of the Provisional IRA political and military campaign.

videos.title: A Hard Act to Follow
videos.overview: Vice President George Bush and Senator Bob Dole are battling for Republican Presidential nomination.

videos.title: The Underclass of 88
videos.overview: The Underclass of 88 In tomorrow's Budget Chancellor is widely expected to announce further tax cuts for better off.

videos.title: Electricity - A Shock in Store
videos.overview: Disturbing new evidence of a connection between electricity and small but significant increases in childhood and adult cancers are mystifying scientists.

videos.title: Church of England - One Foundation?
videos.overview: In Church of England recent passionate arguments about ordination to priesthood of women or of practising homosexuals are symptoms of a much wider debate.

videos.title: Charles, Prince of Conscience
videos.overview: Charles, Prince of Conscience Is Prince of Wales sharpening an impression that he is increasingly out of tune with Thatcherit.

videos.title: Child Abuse: Battering the System
videos.overview: Clare is 4, and her mother fears she has been sexually abused by her father. She's just 30,000 children on local authority 'at risk' register.

videos.title: Israel at 40
videos.overview: Next week, as Israel celebrates 40 years of statehood, Panorama reports on growing-problems of troubled nation.

videos.title: In the Shadow of the Killing Fields
videos.overview: Ten years after Pol Pot 's reign of terror, Cambodians fear horror of killing fields may return.

videos.title: Replacing the Hidden Bomb
videos.overview: Few people know Britain has a class of nuclear bombs other than those carried in Polaris submarines.

videos.title: A Revolution Without Shots
videos.overview: Mikhail Gorbachev has called his attempt to reform Soviet Union 'a revolution without shots'.

videos.title: Selling the Nuclear Dream
videos.overview: When Government privatises electricity industry, everyone in Britain will have chance to buy a stake in nuclear power.

videos.title: Northern Ireland: The Long Peace
videos.overview: After 20 years of unrest, there are first signs of a wind of political change in Northern Ireland.

videos.title: In Wealth We Trust
videos.overview: In his last Budget, Chancellor Lawson gave to those who already had. He cut tax for well-off.

videos.title: The Price of Success?
videos.overview: Britain's South East is beginning to boom. In a crescent around London, new business parks and housing estates are fast expanding.

videos.title: Can We Afford the Doctor?
videos.overview: The death of hole-in-the-heart baby, Matthew Collier has provoked most fundamental review of National Health Service for 40 years.

videos.title: Who Is This Man Dukakis?
videos.overview: As son of Greek immigrants is about to be sent forth as Democratic Party's challenger to recapture American Presidency, Panorama examines credentials of Michael Dukakis.

videos.title: Hot Property
videos.overview: It involves estate agents, valuers and solicitors as well as purchasers, and it's happening both because mortgages are so easily available and because bodies set up to monitor house sales seem unable to cope with buying market.

videos.title: Labour's Agonising Reappraisal
videos.overview: At a time when Opposition should have been making capital of Government's difficulties.

videos.title: Jam Today, Jam Tomorrow?
videos.overview: By year 2000, there will be up to 30 per cent more cars on road. Peter Taylor examines ways of getting out of jam and interviews Secretary of State The Rt Hon Paul Channon.

videos.title: Piper Alpha: The Human Price of Oil
videos.overview: In July, 167 men were killed in world's worst ever oil disaster. Jane Corbin talks to crucial eyewitnesses aboard Piper Alpha that nigbt.

videos.title: A Class Apart
videos.overview: One-hundred-and-eighty children have just begun term at most controversial school in Britain, brand new City Technology College in Solihull.

videos.title: Violent Britain - The Hurd Instinct
videos.overview: On eve of Conservative Party Conference, Home Secretary Rt Hon Douglas Hurd MP is preparing for his toughest challenges of year.

videos.title: The SAS
videos.overview: An investigation into the role of the SAS in Northern Ireland.

videos.title: Choosing the Future - The Genetic Revolution
videos.overview: Using latest DNA technology, scientists are identifying genes which help to determine kind of people we are.

videos.title: Pakistan: Paying for a Holy War
videos.overview: Pakistan has been chief backer of Afghan guerrillas in their Holy War against Soviet army.

videos.title: The Tories: Friends of the Earth?
videos.overview: Mrs Thatcher claims Conservatives are green at heart. The local authorities monitoring Britain's booming waste industry have yet to be convinced.

videos.title: Adios General Pinochet?
videos.overview: After 15 years, people of Chile have voted to get rid of General Pinochet. But his dictatorship continues for next year-and-a-half as a nation, divided by hatred, tries to move towards democracy.

videos.title: Europe: My Way or Theirs?
videos.overview: On eve of Summit of Common Market Leaders, Fred Emery reports on battle for future of Europe after 1992.

videos.title: Council Housing: The Last Frontier
videos.overview: Council estates are Conservatives' next political battlefield. Once, council housing, subsidised and secure, symbolised Welfare State.

videos.title: The Shadow of the Swastika
videos.overview: Half a century after war, hunting down of old Nazis has never been more intense. In America, Canada and Israel, Nazis and their collaborators are facing trial.

videos.title: How Free Is Britain?
videos.overview: Peter Taylor asks whether a decade of Conservative government has eroded or enhanced democratic liberties in the UK.

videos.title: President Bush - Challenging the Future
videos.overview: In four days, George Bush becomes the 41st President of the United States, taking office at a time of momentous change in the structure of world power.

videos.title: Children in Need
videos.overview: This year looks set to be a record year for charity appeals, not only for the Third World but for poor children in Britain.

videos.title: The Killer Inside
videos.overview: There's growing concern that Britain's prisons are a breeding ground for AIDS. Senior prison workers warn that smuggled drugs are widespread and many prisoners continue to share syringes and needles.

videos.title: Factory Fresh: The Food Revolution
videos.overview: It began as an 'epidemic' of salmonella in eggs. It frightened consumers, cost egg producers dear, and lost Mrs. Edwina Currie her job. Now it has put the record and future of British farming on trial.

videos.title: Inside the Ayatollah's Iran
videos.overview: Ruled by an Islamic government, where the aged Ayatollah Khomenei still holds the key to power and the future, Iran still shows the scars of failure in war and is beset by rumours of executions and internal strife.

videos.title: Will You Still Feed Me?
videos.overview: Polly Toynbee reports on the divide between rich and poor old people in the UK. Some feel life has never been better, while many on the state pension are finding it hard to make ends meet, especially if they are coping with elderly or disabled spouses.

videos.title: The Tender Trap
videos.overview: By August, every council in England and Wales will have to start putting six essential services out to tender. Will the home owner get better value for money or will the quality of services decline?

videos.title: Death in the Rainforest
videos.overview: The murder of Chico Mendes , the Brazilian rubber-tappers' leader and defender of the Amazon rainforest has focused world attention on the violent conflict over the future of the Amazon.

videos.title: NHS Plc? - What's in It for Patients?
videos.overview: The Government has embarked on most radical reforms to National Health Service in its history.

videos.title: Sent from Heaven - Sold on Earth
videos.overview: Mrs. Thatcher says that water privatisation has not been handled well. As the Government redoubles its campaign to sell the idea to the public, Panorama asks what's in it for the consumer?

videos.title: Disarming the Alliance: The Soviet Peace Offensive
videos.overview: Tomorrow NATO celebrates its 40th anniversary. But the Western Alliance, forged in the Cold War, now faces the challenge of the new Soviet peace offensive.

videos.title: The Condor Conspiracy
videos.overview: Panorama Episode featuring Jane Corbin on threat posed by Argentinian Condor Missile Programme.

videos.title: Whose Law Is It Anyway?
videos.overview: The High Court is closed today. For the first time in history, judges have downed wigs to debate what they suspect may be a threat to justice itself. On trial are the Government's plans to reform the legal profession.

videos.title: No Spring in Prague
videos.overview: From Czechoslovakia where Soviet tanks crushed the experiment of 'Communism with a human face' in 1968. Today the Government in Prague, paralysed by the fear of change, has embarked on a new repression.

videos.title: Ten Years' Hard Labour
videos.overview: Ten years ago the last Labour government was defeated by the Tories under Margaret Thatcher. What has been the impact of Thatcherism on the Labour party? Thatcher once declared that her aim was to 'eliminate socialism'. Has she succeeded?

videos.title: Football - Safe in Their Hands?
videos.overview: Whatever the outcome of the inquiry into the Hillsborough tragedy, Britain's worst sporting disaster has already provoked a crisis of confidence in our national game.

videos.title: Punching Judy
videos.overview: Latest Police figures show an increase in crimes of domestic violence, unmatched since records began. One in four assaults is by a man on a wife or girlfriend. In London alone, a thousand battered women ask the police for help each week.

videos.title: University Challenge
videos.overview: Alan Young comes from Bedlington near Newcastle. His father was a miner, his mother works at the local hospital. Alan is one of Oxford's brightest mathematicians. But will there be any more like him?

videos.title: Alaska: Oil on the Rocks
videos.overview: When the Exxon Valdez ran aground off the coast of Alaska last March, it was the worst oil spill in American history. Now the implications may affect the future of America's entire oil industry.

videos.title: Lady Porter - The Pursuit of Power
videos.overview: The leader of Westminster's Conservative council, Lady Porter, one of a new breed of town-hall Tories. Lady Porter's reputation has been in the doldrums since her policy of selling Westminster's cemeteries to developers for a pittance.

videos.title: Getting the Message Across
videos.overview: In the 10 yrs since Thatcher came to power the bill for Gov't advertising has doubled to E150 million. The water privatisation advertising campaign has cost more than that of Nescafe Gold Blend, Persil, Guinness and Coca Cola put together.

videos.title: Solidarity - Taking the Reins of Power
videos.overview: This September, Poland is living through some of the most momentous days in its history. For the first time in Eastern Europe for 40 years, a non-Communist Prime Minister leads the Government.

videos.title: Happy Families
videos.overview: One in three marriages ends in divorce. A quarter of all babies are now born to mothers who have never married at all. Without a father as a breadwinner, most single mothers and children end up on social security.

videos.title: Lockerbie: An Avoidable Tragedy
videos.overview: As the hunt to bring to justice the murderers of 270 passengers and crew continues into its tenth month, Gavin Hewitt has traced the story from Scotland to the United States, to the Middle East and West Germany.

videos.title: Afghanistan: The Squandered Victory
videos.overview: When the Soviet army withdrew from Afghanistan last February, the regime in Kabul was expected to fall to the Afghan rebels within weeks. But, ten months later, victory in the Holy War against the Communists has degenerated into civil war.

videos.title: Follow My Leader
videos.overview: Anthony Howard reports for BBC Panorama into the thoughts and stratagems of the Conservative powerbrokers, from 1989.

videos.title: British Rail: The Ultimate Sell-Off
videos.overview: Fred Emery reports on reaction round the country to the many changes already affecting British Rail services in what's being seen as the run-up to privatisation.

videos.title: Crack Crisis - Is Britain Next?
videos.overview: Crack; the drug which President Bush says is turning American cities into battle zones. Is now starting to appear on some British streets. One of President Bush's top advisers warned that Britain could have a similar epidemic to New York.

videos.title: Gorbachev: Reaping the Whirlwind - The Poisoned Land
videos.overview: From the Aral Sea, evidence of a catastrophe that rivals Chernobyl. The planning decisions of the Brezhnev years have left a great many facing disease, deformity and death. As the sea dries up, the ecology of the region disintegrates.

videos.title: Gorbachev: Reaping the Whirlwind - Bloody Sunday
videos.overview: In Tblisi, the capital of Soviet Georgia, troops encircled a crowd of peaceful demonstrators and attacked them with truncheons, entrenching tools and gas. 20 people were killed - more than 3/4 were women - and over 500 taken to hospital.

videos.title: The Boys on B Wing
videos.overview: How is it that every year 1,500 teenage boys - all 16 years old or younger - can be locked up in British prisons, two to a cell, 20 hours a day, on remand sometimes for offences as trivial as absconding and car theft?

videos.title: What Future for Thatcherism?
videos.overview: With the shock waves of the recent political crisis still reverberating through the Government, is Mrs. Thatcher's famous conviction and single-mindedness now more of a liability than an asset to the Tories?

videos.title: Allies in Arms
videos.overview: Investigates the S.A.-Ulster Alliance in arms.

videos.title: Triumph Over Tyranny
videos.overview: After fleeing the capital as revolutionary fervour spread, Romanian President Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife were captured and returned to Bucharest to face the revolution's summary justice on Christmas Day 1989.

videos.title: Suffering for a Solution
videos.overview: David Lomax reports on how patients are suffering as a result of the 1990 ambulance dispute.

videos.title: Bunking Off
videos.overview: Every day this term more than 200,000 pupils will play truant from Britain's schools. In London alone a quarter of all 15-year-olds will be missing from class.

videos.title: The Winter of Perestroika
videos.overview: As crises mount for President Gorbachev, what about the Russians - the people who will ultimately determine the fate of his revolution?

videos.title: The Police: In for Questioning
videos.overview: Britain's police are facing a crisis of public confidence. In the wake of the Guildford Four case, the break up of the West Midlands Crime Squad and the Wapping report, there is a widespread fear that the police bend the rules.

videos.title: Ulster's Regiment - A Question of Loyalty?
videos.overview: August's shooting of a young Catholic, Loughlin Maginn, was the 2,744th murder since the N. Ireland troubles began. But it will be remembered as the killing which triggered off a damaging row between the governments of London and Dublin.

videos.title: Who's Afraid of Germany?
videos.overview: East Germans vote next Sunday in their first free elections in over 50 years. But already the hundreds of thousands who have voted with their feet, moving to the west, have settled the issue in favour of 'One Fatherland'.

videos.title: Poll Taxing Their Loyalty
videos.overview: In England and Wales 38 million people are about to receive their first poll tax bills - many will be higher than Government predictions.

videos.title: Concrete v. Countryside
videos.overview: In the 90s, Britain will need new roads, houses and industrial developments if it is to prosper in Europe. But birds, plants and animals are under increasing pressure as the concrete spreads.

videos.title: Falling Through the Net
videos.overview: The very poor in Britain live at the margin. Any crisis, from a house burning down to something as everyday as a child needing new shoes, can push them over the edge. All they can turn to in an emergency is the Government's social fund.

videos.title: House Prices, Home Truths
videos.overview: More than three million people have joined Britain's army of homeowners since Mrs. Thatcher came to power. But for many, high mortgage rates and the slump in property prices have turned the dream of home ownership into a nightmare.

videos.title: The Red Army Revolution
videos.overview: The mighty Red Army that Lenin created to defend the Motherland is coming home from camps across Eastern Europe. But it is returning to an uncertain future.

videos.title: Doctoring the Reforms
videos.overview: 18 months ago, the Gov't launched a radical reform of the NHS. It wanted to turn a £20 billion state monolith into an internal market that would offer its 'customers', the patients, a better service, choice, and better value for money.

videos.title: The Crimes of the Comrades
videos.overview: All over eastern Europe, dark secrets from the past are being unearthed. Many countries face the dilemma of what to do with the former communist dictators and their thugs from state security.

videos.title: The Big Heat
videos.overview: Steve Bradshaw reports on the effects of global warming.

videos.title: Rioting for Rights?
videos.overview: One self-confessed ringleader of the Strangeways riot has claimed to Panorama that the disturbance was originally planned as a protest against the prison regime.

videos.title: Selling Our Schools
videos.overview: As the Government's changes to the education system start to take effect, how well are Britain's schools coping? Roisin McAuley reports on the effects on one typical secondary, Campion School in Leamington, Warwickshire.

videos.title: Selling Socialism
videos.overview: With Westminster rife with pre-election fever and Labour ahead in the opinion polls, the Leader of the Opposition, the Rt Hon Neil Kinnock , MP, gives his first major television interview of the year.

videos.title: A Woman's Work
videos.overview: After a rather difficult political year, the Conservatives are now preparing to fight their fourth election campaign under the leadership of Margaret Thatcher. It looks as if it may be the toughest yet for her as well as for her party.

videos.title: Saddam's Secret Arms Ring
videos.overview: How did the west allow Saddam Hussein to build up his terrifying arsenal of weapons? Jane Corbin reveals the scale of Saddam's arms production network in Britain, Germany and America.

videos.title: Saddam's Fifth Column
videos.overview: To many Palestinians, Saddam Hussein is a new saviour. Panorama analyses the Saddam-fever that is sweeping through Jordan and the West Bank into Israel. Robin Denselow reports.

videos.title: Uncle Sam v. Saddam
videos.overview: David Dimbleby and Tom Mangold report from America on the latest developments in the Gulf crisis. Is a compromise still possible? How long will the American people be prepared to support such a massive commitment of American forces?

videos.title: The Gulf in Our Defences
videos.overview: Britain's defences were undergoing their most drastic review for over a generation when Iraq provoked the Gulf crisis. Fred Emery reports on the controversy raging inside the Ministry of Defence.

videos.title: Labour's Liverpool Nightmare
videos.overview: Reporter Steve Bradshaw investigates the legacy of Militant Tendency in Liverpool.

videos.title: Who Pays for the Party?
videos.overview: Gavin Hewitt has been examining who actually pays for the Conservative Party. Why do individuals and companies give and what do they expect in return?

videos.title: The White Tribe of Africa: Part 1 - Drowning in Blood
videos.overview: An examination of the cause and effect of the savage violence which has been sweeping South Africa, a threat to the peace process which, in Nelson Mandela 's words, could leave the country 'drowning in blood'.

videos.title: The White Tribe of Africa: Part 2 - No Way Back
videos.overview: President F W de Klerk's promise to abolish all race laws and share power with the black majority has set white against white in South Africa. David Dimbleby meets some who are reconciled to change and others who are determined to resist.

videos.title: Sins of the Fathers
videos.overview: In an attempt to make the family a lasting commitment, the Government is changing the law to track down fathers who abandon their families so they can be forced to pay maintenance.

videos.title: The Price of Freedom
videos.overview: David Dimbleby in Potsdam presents a debate with representatives from several European countries on their adjustment to the new freedoms one year on from the fall of the Berlin Wall.

videos.title: Mr. Major's Medicine
videos.overview: The Chancellor of the Exchequer's decision to take Britain into the Exchange Rate Mechanism provoked short-lived euphoria. Now the British economy has to conquer inflation and compete in Europe with a fixed rate for the pound.

videos.title: The Cruellest Thing
videos.overview: Fred Emery presents a Panorama special about the demise of British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, looking at the final week of her premiership.

videos.title: International Aids Day
videos.overview: As the world marks international Aids day, Panorama reports on the relentless spread of the disease into the general population. The authorities are still not encouraging those who think they might have the virus to get tested.

videos.title: Mr Ridley's Europe
videos.overview: Anthony Howard accompanies former cabinet minister Nicholas Ridley on a journey around Europe, highlighting his opinions of the European Community in the light of recent political events.

videos.title: Guildford: The Untold Story
videos.overview: The Department of Public Prosecutions is considering whether to prosecute a group of junior Surrey detectives who are alleged to have fabricated the confessions of some of the Guildford Four.

videos.title: The Chances Of Averting War
videos.overview: Reports on central issues of day at home and abroad. As Gulf crisis reaches a critical stage and UN deadline for Iraq to withdraw from Kuwait runs out, Panorama assesses chances of averting war.

videos.title: Project Babylon
videos.overview: The full story of Saddam Hussein 's supergun is revealed. It began as one scientist's dream.

videos.title: Episode 7
videos.overview: While world has been distracted by Gulf crisis, momentous political events have been taking place in Soviet Union.

videos.title: Episode 8
videos.overview: As foreign ministers gather in Brussels to discuss next steps towards political union, Panorama examines impact of Gulf crisis on Europe.

videos.title: Episode 9
videos.overview: David Dimbleby presents analysis and discussion of the latest events in the Gulf.

videos.title: Episode 10
videos.overview: On eve of Budget, Panorama asks whether recession is doing lasting damage to Britain's industrial fabric.

videos.title: America's Secret War
videos.overview: Intelligence gathering played a vital role in military success of Allies in Gulf War.

videos.title: Race Hate Uk
videos.overview: In 1991 Panorama investigated rise of racist violence in UK and role of openly racist British National Party.

videos.title: The Major Question
videos.overview: John Major's honeymoon is over. Now he's faced with tough decisions on poll tax, economy and timing of next election.

videos.title: The Cancer Lottery
videos.overview: Every cancer patient wants best treatment, but finding it may be a matter of chance.

videos.title: Beyond the Poll Tax
videos.overview: In week when millions vote in local elections and government unveils its replacement for poll tax, spotlight is on local government.

videos.title: Cold Warrior - The Story of James Jesus Angleton
videos.overview: Tonight's special edition traces extraordinary career of James Jesus Angleton, most famous spycatcher of them all.

videos.title: Scuttling British Shipbuilders
videos.overview: Investigation into the collapse of British shipbuilding, with reporter Fred Emery.

videos.title: Escape from Tiananmen
videos.overview: Two years after massacre in Tiananmen Square, Panorama reveals story of Yellow Bird.

videos.title: Rivals for Russia
videos.overview: David Dimbleby presents a special program from Moscow in week of first free election since Revolution.

videos.title: The Dream of Kurdistan
videos.overview: After refugee crisis, what hope is there for Kurds of attaining their own homeland?

videos.title: Making a Killing?
videos.overview: In aftermath of Gulf War, western leaders say it is time for world's major weapons producers to cut back on arms sales.

videos.title: Out of Sight, Out of Mind
videos.overview: Government plan to close Britain's top security hospitals.

videos.title: Labour Pains
videos.overview: But post-war Labour prime ministers have faced same persistent problems: sterling crises, pressures on spending, strained relations with ' unions, and internal party 4 strife.

videos.title: The Battle for Britain's Defences
videos.overview: As Britain's armed forces wait to hear who's going to be on receiving end of government's military cutbacks, David Dimbleby chairs a special debate on future of our defences.

videos.title: Lethal Force
videos.overview: John Ware investigates a chain of recent killings by British soldiers in Northern Ireland.

videos.title: ICI: Hanson's Choice
videos.overview: A state of war exists between ICI, Britain's top chemical company, and Hanson plc, over the prospect of Britain's largest ever takeover.

videos.title: Kuwait: The Victims of Victory
videos.overview: The first of three special programs about Gulf War and its aftermath. Jane Corbin returns to Kuwait one year after Iraq's invasion.

videos.title: Iraq: Saddam the Survivor
videos.overview: Did Saddam really lose Gulf War? In second of three special Panorama documentaries about war and its aftermath.

videos.title: The Allies: In the Eye of the Storm
videos.overview: The last of three reports about Gulf War and its aftermath. Interviews with military commanders and previously unseen Pentagon film cast new light on some crucial.

videos.title: Goodbye USSR
videos.overview: As the Soviet Union breaks up, reporter Gavin Hewitt explores the death of a superpower. Will its end be bloody or peaceful? And will the desire for revenge against communists, and renewed ethnic feuding cause further bloodshed?

videos.title: Episode 35
videos.overview: On eve of Conservative Party Conference, BBC's political editor John Cole assesses current state of John Major's party.

videos.title: The Halcion Nightmare
videos.overview: Tom Mangold reveals astonishing facts behind decision to remove a drug associated with serious psychiatric disturbances including violent and suicidal behavior.

videos.title: No Surrender, No Progress
videos.overview: This summer, hopes for a political settlement in Northern Ireland flickered then died. But Secretary of State for Northern Ireland Peter Brooke refuses to give up the search for peace.

videos.title: Deprived or Depraved?
videos.overview: Last month, several British cities were blighted by rioting, and politicians and church leaders cast around for explanations for civil unrest. And whether the riots represent a failure of the Government's policies in deprived areas.

videos.title: The Bank That Didn't Add Up
videos.overview: When last July Bank of England co-ordinated action to close down BCCI, world's largest international banks.

videos.title: Class Wars
videos.overview: The Government has renewed its onslaught on "trendy educationalists", claiming they have spread a mania for equality through Britain's schools. Panorama reports on the war for the hearts and minds of Britain's schoolchildren.

videos.title: Episode 42
videos.overview: Has Thatcherite housing agenda led to a housing crisis, with family homes being repossessed because of over-extended mortgages and too little money going into public housing?

videos.title: Episode 43
videos.overview: In week that European Community leaders meet in Maastricht to discuss political and monetary union

videos.title: Risky Business
videos.overview: King's Cross, Zeebrugge, Piper Alpha - more than a thousand people died in the big disasters of the late 80s. Yet after most disasters and deaths at work, company managements escape unpunished.

videos.title: Getting Rid of Granny
videos.overview: The Prime Minister praised the NHS for the treatment his parents received when they were ill in their old age. But many health authorities are now cutting back or even abandoning long-stay beds, moving the elderly to private nursing homes.

videos.title: Nuclear Nightmare
videos.overview: The collapse of Soviet Union has left thousands of nuclear warheads, vast amounts of plutonium and entire cities full of scientists who know how to make nuclear weapons: what happens to them now?

videos.title: The Third Man
videos.overview: As the General Election approaches, opinion polls suggest an increasing likelihood of the result being a hung Parliament. If so, the balance of power may be held by Paddy Ashdown , the leader of the Liberal Democrats.

videos.title: Bush's Domestic Storm
videos.overview: Next week George Bush sets out on the long electoral road to a 2nd term in the White House. But America is ill disposed to reward the President for his foreign policy successes. The campaign spotlight has focused on the ailing US economy.

videos.title: Episode 6
videos.overview: As the opinion polls indicate that-half the Scottish electorate now favours independence, David Dimbleby chairs a debate from Edinburgh on the future of Scotland's government.

videos.title: Unsafe Convictions
videos.overview: Three men are serving life sentences for gruesome murder of a Cardiff prostitute. Tom Mangold investigates some of methods used by police in a case led to longest murder trial in British history.

videos.title: Crisis at the Coalface
videos.overview: Since the miners' strike 7 yrs ago, productivity in Britain's mines has soared and efficiency improved beyond expectations. But there have been pit closures and redundancies as the coal industry has felt the chill blast of market forces.

videos.title: The Slide Into Slump
videos.overview: Now that it is officially admitted that Britain's current economic recession is the longest since the Second World War, a bitter debate has broken out about its origins.

videos.title: The Chancellors' Debate
videos.overview: David Dimbleby chairs a debate on one of the issues crucial to the outcome of the imminent General Election.

videos.title: Leaders: Liberal Democrats
videos.overview: David Dimbleby face-to-face with party leaders. Tonight: Paddy Ashdown, Leader of Liberal Democrats.

videos.title: Leaders: Labour Party
videos.overview: David Dimbleby face-to-face in live interviews with party leaders. Tonight: Neil Kinnock, Leader of Labour Party.

videos.title: Leaders: Conservative Party
videos.overview: The Prime Minister and Leader of the Conservative Party, John Major, is interviewed live by David Dimbleby. Can the Conservatives win the election despite the longest economic recession since the war?

videos.title: Episode 14
videos.overview: What are the implications of the election result for the nation and for its political parties? David Dimbleby and the Panorama team assess last Thursday's poll.

videos.title: Not a Drop to Drink
videos.overview: Summer has not yet arrived but already large areas of southern Britain are subject to hosepipe bans and other restrictions on use of water.

videos.title: The House Party's Over
videos.overview: Are golden days over for British home owners? Reporter John Plender looks at whether in future owning a house will still be a sure way of doubling your money or whether.

videos.title: Citizen Major's Charter
videos.overview: The Citizen's Charter, which John Major launched as Tories' "big idea" for 90s, is rapidly breeding mini-charters setting new standards for most public services.

videos.title: The South Strikes Back
videos.overview: At Earth Summit in Rio this week, tax payers in rich countries like Britain will be asked to pay billions of pounds to save world from environmental disaster.

videos.title: Episode 20
videos.overview: Are police now calling a truce in war on drugs? Fewer users are being prosecuted, but does this mean there is a move towards a decriminalisation of drugs use?.

videos.title: Episode 21
videos.overview: As Israel prepares to go to the polls, the Middle East peace process hangs in the balance. Jane Corbin reports on how the Israeli voters will affect the prospect for peace.

videos.title: Pension Funds
videos.overview: In wake of Maxwell scandal, there are fears that pension funds are vulnerable to theft and sharp practice by people who run them.

videos.title: Hong Kong
videos.overview: In a few days' time, Britain's last governor will arrive in Hong Kong - in preparation for handing the colony over to China. Can Chris Patten save the way of life of its people, or will it fall prey to the regime in Peking?

videos.title: Dollars, Deals and the Old Guard
videos.overview: Almost a year after abortive coup against Gorbachev, ghost of communism still haunts former Soviet Union.

videos.title: AIDS
videos.overview: New fears about an Aids epidemic in the heterosexual community have been raised by recent highly publicised cases. Tom Mangold looks at new evidence on how Aids spreads among heterosexuals, and whether current health policies are effective

videos.title: The Dentists' Revolt
videos.overview: Is free dental care in danger of becoming a thing of past? As dentists threaten to withdraw from NHS over Government's attempts to regulate their fees, Steve Bradshaw reports on widening gap between private and NHS dentistry.

videos.title: America's Killing Question
videos.overview: Supporters of death penalty in America used to claim it was a deterrent to violent crime.

videos.title: The Plutonium Business
videos.overview: Britain is poised to become a major player in an international trade in deadly plutonium.

videos.title: For Those in Peril
videos.overview: Forced to remain in harbour against their will and obliged to throw almost half their catch back into sea, British fishermen are angrier than at any time since "cod war" of early 1970s.

videos.title: One Rule for the Bosses
videos.overview: Despite the recession, the pay of Britain's company directors is rising faster than ever. How do they justify double-figure increases? Michael Crick finds out who sets the boss's pay and whether there is a better way.

videos.title: For Fools and Horses?
videos.overview: Horse racing in Britain is in crisis. Is it because it's not run in a business-like way or because bookies aren't paying their fair share?

videos.title: Britain's Rural Revolution
videos.overview: New payments to farmers to produce less food will result in an area of farmland bigger than Devon being released. Will this lead to widespread dereliction? Should the land be used for housing and industry or returned to nature?

videos.title: Episode 34
videos.overview: On the eve of the Conservative Party conference, another in-depth investigation and analysis of current events with the Panorama team.

videos.title: Episode 35
videos.overview: Recent events have shaken the foundations of the EC. As the 12 gather for a summit in Britain this week, Martha Kearney looks at the view from France and Germany and asks whether these nations will create a premier league in Europe.

videos.title: The Refugee Trail
videos.overview: This year, hundreds of thousands of people will be smuggled into the west from the former communist states of eastern Europe. Nisha Pillai reports on this crime which is fast becoming a European growth industry.

videos.title: The Comeback Kid
videos.overview: Bill Clinton has suffered the most sustained attacks on a candidate's character in recent American history, over sex, drugs and the draft. Yet he goes into next week's election with the best prospects a Democrat has had in 16 years.

videos.title: Why Pay for Auntie?
videos.overview: The future of some popular BBC tv shows, from Eldorado to the Generation Game, is under scrutiny. Why should viewers pay a licence for the kind of programmes that may be widely available on rival channels in the 90s?

videos.title: In the Name of Satan?
videos.overview: Animal sacrifice, child sexual abuse, cannibalism and murder: crimes committed, claim some, in the name of Satan. According to one estimate, satanic ritual abuse is rife in every town in Britain, but is this myth or reality?

videos.title: Crack UK: Britain's War on Cocaine
videos.overview: Crack cocaine is most dangerous illegal drugs ever to reach Britain. The intense pleasure it gives soon leads to addiction, and a deadly spiral of depression and destructiveness.

videos.title: UK Ltd: The Arming of Iraq
Wanna Buy a Railway?
videos.overview: Under Mrs Thatcher, ministers said they meant to privatise British Rail, but left it in public ownership. Now John Major's government intends to show how radical it is, by de-nationalising the industry.

videos.title: The Great Pit Disaster
videos.overview: The economic case for closing 31 pits and putting 30,000 miners on the dole was "unanswerable", the government said. But public outcry forced them to order a review.

videos.title: The Road to Hope
videos.overview: On 20 January, Bill Clinton will become the first Democratic president of the United States for 12 years. Peter Jay, who was Britain's ambassador to the USA during the Carter administration, examines the mood of the country.

videos.title: The Bitter-Enders: Part 1
videos.overview: First of a two-part report. As South Africa prepares for the coming election, David Dimbleby talks to President F W De Klerk and to Nelson Mandela.

videos.title: The Bitter-Enders: Part 2
videos.overview: Second of a two-part report. David Dimbleby talks to President F W De Klerk and to Nelson Mandela, and assesses the chances of the white and black population reaching a settlement which will put an end to the confrontation and bloodshed.

videos.title: Monarchy, Magic and Citizen Major
videos.overview: This year sees the 40th anniversary of the Queen's coronation. What is the prospect for the monarchy today, and what place is there for its ancient magic in Citizen Major's Britain? Vivian White reports.

videos.title: Whose Mind Is It Anyway?
videos.overview: A month after being discharged from a psychiatric hospital, Tracey Evans killed her children in what she called an "act of love". Her husband believes it wouldn't have happened if she had received more supervision when she left hospital.

videos.title: Arming for Islam
videos.overview: A new military power looks set to overtake Saddam's Iraq. In the Islamic republic of Iran the heirs of Ayatollah Khomeini are spending billions on arms. Jane Corbin investigates that Iran is trying to get weapons of mass destruction.

videos.title: A Class Apart
videos.overview: The dramatic increase in the numbers of children expelled from school is causing problems for a Government already grappling with public anxiety over juvenile crime. Many children now receive as little as one hour's education a week.

videos.title: The Peace Penalty
videos.overview: As the post-Cold War military cuts go deeper, Britain faces hundreds of thousands of job losses in the defence sector, bringing despair to areas of previously high employment.

videos.title: Underclass in Purdah
videos.overview: Nisha Pillai reveals the emergence of a Muslim underclass among Pakistanis and Bangladeshis and looks at the dangers and dilemmas it throws up.

videos.title: Fair Cops
videos.overview: Britain's top policemen now admit that their old Dixon of Dock Green image was always a myth - and that in the battle to convict criminals, truth has often been the first casualty. Steve Bradshaw reports.

videos.title: Dumping Granny
videos.overview: By the end of this decade more than a million people in Britain will be over 85. Some families are already abandoning relatives when they become very old and frail, Margaret Gilmore investigates.

videos.title: Pack of Lies
videos.overview: Tom Mangold investigates the tobacco companies' conspiracy to cover up research that helps prove the link between smoking, cancer and other diseases; and how the industry decided to drop the successful marketing of a safer cigarette.

videos.title: Lucky to Have a Job
videos.overview: Are workers in Britain being exploited by bosses who say they are lucky to have a job? Thousands are being forced to work longer hours for less pay. Others are sacked for no reason and there is nothing in the law to protect them.

videos.title: The Beast of Corleone
videos.overview: For more than ten years, Salvatore Riina was the Godfather of the Mafia, the world's largest criminal organisation. After 23 years on the run, he was arrested. Does his arrest mark a turning point in the struggle against organised crime?

videos.title: The Gene Genie
videos.overview: The race is on to discover the genes that determine people's susceptibility to illness and disease. Billions of dollars are available in the new market for genetic testing but the human costs of such advances may outweigh the benefits.

videos.title: Secrets of the Citadel
videos.overview: A report from Aldermaston, Britain's top-secret nuclear weapons factory, known as the Citadel. Nuclear weapons are being constructed in buildings that were condemned 15 years ago by an independent inquiry into the Atomic Weapons Facility.

videos.title: Lloyd's Last Chance
videos.overview: Lloyd's of London - the most famous insurance market in the world - is in crisis. After hurricanes, terrorism and tanker disasters losses run into billions, and legal actions alleging negligence and fraud abound.

videos.title: Bad Medicine
videos.overview: Can hospitals be trusted to provide the best possible care? Panorama offers evidence that some cannot and that differences in financing and treatment mean that certain hospitals and surgeons are more effective than others

videos.title: The Gift of God or Human Torment?
videos.overview: Thousands of Catholic priests have left active service to marry. Sex scandals involving American archbishops have rocked Rome and led Pope John Paul II to concede that the public's trust in the church and priestly morale is being eroded.

videos.title: Wessex Man
videos.overview: Wessex Regional Health Authority is said to have wasted tens of millions of pounds on installing a computer system that had to be abandoned. Vivian White uncovers the people and companies responsible for squandering vital NHS funds.

videos.title: The Dental AIDS Mystery
videos.overview: Florida dentist Dr David Acer has been held responsible for transmitting the deadly HIV virus to six of his patients. Two have died. Yet after a two-year inquiry no one can find out how it happened.

videos.title: The Rape of Justice
videos.overview: In cases of sexual assault, are the courts too lenient when it comes to sentencing? Will the government respond to public disquiet? Deborah Davies reports.

videos.title: To Catch a Thief
videos.overview: Is Britain becoming a nation of vigilantes? Peter Godwin investigates a growing trend of DIY crime-fighters - some legal, others definitely not.

videos.title: The Whole Truth
videos.overview: A succession of miscarriages of justice have brought about tougher measures to protect the accused in criminal cases. But have the scales of justice tilted too far in favour of the defendants?

videos.title: An Ordinary Boy
videos.overview: Two IRA bombs in a crowded Warrington shopping centre on 20 March this year killed 3-year-old Jonathan Ball immediately; 12-year-old Tim Parry died five days later. Steve Bradshaw reports.

videos.title: The Norway Channel
videos.overview: The story of a Norwegian couple who had formed a secret channel between the Israelis and the Palestinian Liberation Organisation.

videos.title: Babies on Benefit
videos.overview: Michele is 22 and expecting the fifth of her babies she's had by two different fathers. Janet lied to the authorities to gain extra welfare benefits for her children. Panorama investigates the cost to the state of young single motherhood.

videos.title: Cut Adrift
videos.overview: "It's very easy when you're in politics - to find yourself cut adrift from the everyday concerns of people in the country" John Major tells Panorama. Huw Edwards asks party members whether Mr Major can dispel the doubts on his leadership.

videos.title: Pensioned Off
videos.overview: Stephen Bradshaw reports that the state pays out billions of pounds in benefits to pensioners who don't need the money. Would it not make sense to target their pension money at the millions of poor old people who desperately need it?

videos.title: The Sinful Messiah
videos.overview: John Penycate examines the Branch Davidians and David Koresh's bizarre cocktail of religion, violence and sexual abuse, and reveals the story of the US government's role In the Waco shooting, siege and final conflagration

videos.title: Securing a Headline
videos.overview: With the Jamie Bulger trial about to start, and public concern about child criminals in the news, the Government is promising tough new policies to deal with the worst offenders. They plan new sentences and new lock-ups for 12-14 year-olds

videos.title: Water - Profits and Poverty
videos.overview: A few yrs ago water charges were a small item on the rates bill, but now they're increasing up to 8 times the rate of inflation. While water chiefs and shareholders enjoy a profits bonanza, water poverty threatens millions of families.

videos.title: A Very British Folly
videos.overview: This week the government is expected to give the final go-ahead to Thorp, a nuclear "laundry" meant to clean the used fuel of a new generation of atomic power stations. But is Thorp really needed? Correspondent Ian Breech reports.

videos.title: Race, Violence and the Law
videos.overview: New government figures suggest that racially motivated attacks in Britain are far more frequent than was previously estimated. Only a small proportion are reported, however, and even fewer reach the courts. Margaret Gilmore reports.

videos.title: Getting Away with Murder
videos.overview: Stephen Bradshaw reports from Foca, in Bosnia, where innocent civilians have been victims of war crimes, and of history's broken promises, and he names local politicians who failed to intervene and stop these crimes.

videos.title: Nose to Tail
videos.overview: Will government plans to spend £23 billion on Britain's roads ease traffic jams or encourage more people to take to their cars? Reporter John Penycate talks to people affected by schemes such as the widening of the M25 and M62.

videos.title: Current Fears
videos.overview: Simon Studholme died of leukaemia in 1992. His bedroom was next to electricity meter and outside house stands an electricity substation.

videos.title: For the Sake of the Children
videos.overview: With 1994 designated Year of Family, it is disturbing trends emerging from 1980s show more children than ever will go.

videos.title: Battling for Air
videos.overview: Two thousand people die of asthma each year in Britain. The number of sufferers is growing, and blame is being leveled at air pollution.

videos.title: Who's Sorry Now
videos.overview: Five years ago government created personal pensions industry -and a big problem. The government now promises industry's system of "self-regulation" is to be tightened up, but reporter Vivian White reveals that.

videos.title: The Sacrifice Zone
videos.overview: America began to conduct atomic tests at Yucca Flats in Nevada soon after Second World War, and "down-winders" across border in Utah were repeatedly told they were safe.

videos.title: Truth Is a Difficult Concept
videos.overview: The Scott Inquiry into exports to Iraq has put inner workings of government on public display as never.

videos.title: Breast Cancer
videos.overview: An investigation into one of the biggest killers of middle-aged women in Britain - breast cancer. The programme reports on how doctors are either unaware of or are apparently ignoring the latest research on treatment.

videos.title: The Red Peril
videos.overview: After the success of Vladimir Zhirinovsky in Russia's recent elections, Panorama examines the threat to world peace. The strong feelings of national pride and resentment in Russia could form the seed-beds of nationalist aggression.

videos.title: Mandela's Promised Land
videos.overview: In 1987 the BBC's Michael Buerk was refused a renewal of his work permit to report from South Africa - effectively he was expelled, as part of the increasing government clampdown on coverage of the apartheid regime.

videos.title: Gravy Training
videos.overview: Government schemes to train long-term unemployed sound like a good idea but this investigation reveals they are often very expensive, ineffective and merely a way to massage unemployment figures.

videos.title: Seacroft Is Britain
videos.overview: On the South Seacroft estate in Leeds, syringes lie in gutters and drug dealers cruise the streets in fast cars confident the police won't catch them. For the children in this area, drugs are a way of life.

videos.title: Arafat's Historic Return To Jericho
videos.overview: PLO Chairman Arafat "is no Nelson Mandela" according to a Palestinian commentator, but he has agreed to a fundamental change in the way Arab and Jew will live together in the Middle East. Jane Corbin reports.

videos.title: Poison in the Mouth
videos.overview: Are our dental fillings making us ill? Tom Mangold reports on alarming new evidence about amalgam, the substance metal fillings are made of.

videos.title: Grassed! - The Changing Role of the Police Informant
videos.overview: "The police force should not be enticing people to commit crime - And that is what they have been doing," says James Daniels, a small-time villain who claims he was set up by a police informer on a major firearms charge.

videos.title: Salvaging Babies
videos.overview: "If the baby comes out and looks a 'goer', we will try for it" says a doctor to a woman 22 weeks pregnant and starting contractions. Sarah Barclay examines whether it is miraculous or madness to try to save babies born extremely premature.

videos.title: The Landlord's Return
videos.overview: The landlord is back. But is he up to the job? In tonight's programme, Mike Embley investigates the rent revolution - millions of people who've always looked to the state for a home are being forced to go to private landlords.

videos.title: An Act of Man
videos.overview: What is future for Rwandans who survive refugee camps? The United Nations is trying to persuade survivors to return to what is left of their homes in Rwanda but many refugees see little alternative to life of dependency of camps.

videos.title: Golden Handshakes
videos.overview: Why should a company director of two years' standing get a "golden handshake" of half-a-million pounds when a middle manager has to work for 20 years before he or she is offered a year's salary?

videos.title: Blair's Britain
videos.overview: Tonight Panorama introduces Tony Blair, the man behind the rhetoric and headlines. In the town of Southampton, Blair meets the middle England he is said to represent. What does he have to offer? Stephen Bradshaw reports.

videos.title: The Age of Fear
videos.overview: Peter Jay, BBC Economics Editor, looks at job insecurity, issue of 90s. With "a job for life" now an outdated concept, parents fear their children will suffer a drop in their standard of living.

videos.title: The Uneasy Peace
videos.overview: In wake of IRA ceasefire, Panorama reports on mood of Unionist community. A member of unionist Orange Order alleges Northern Ireland has been undergoing IRA "ethnic cleansing" for some time.

videos.title: The Future Is Female
videos.overview: From babyhood to boardroom, women are now set to out-achieve men. Panorama reveals evidence that the future is female - and the weaker sex is now male. Have women won the war of the sexes? Mike Embley reports.

videos.title: The Mr. Nice Guy Murders
videos.overview: He was the boy from the other side of the tracks, poor, black, who made it in a white man's world. The trial of 0J Simpson, an American sporting hero, on charges of murdering his wife and her friend has become the story of the decade.

videos.title: The Greatest Nightmare
videos.overview: Is "the greatest nightmare" of being "old, sick, poor and uncared for" referred to by John Major at the Conservative Party Conference already a reality for thousands of Britain's sick and elderly? Sarah Barclay reports.

videos.title: Ferries - The Fatal Flaw
videos.overview: On 28 September the ferry Estonia sank in minutes in the Baltic Sea with the loss of 900 lives. It was the second major accident involving roll-on roll-off passenger ferries in seven years. Jane Corbin reports.

videos.title: Annus Horribili
videos.overview: In the wake of books, biographies and annus horribili, the monarchy is facing its biggest crisis for half a century. Even establishment circles are now worried that the cracks in the royal facade are beginning to show.

videos.title: Not So Great Railway Journeys
videos.overview: As British Rail is broken up into more than 80 new companies, trains are grinding to a halt with more cancellations and late trains, leaving even more passengers waiting at the station.

videos.title: Bad Blood
videos.overview: Tonight's programme investigates the spread of Hepatitis C through contaminated blood. Britain was the last country in Europe to screen its blood donors for the potentially fatal virus, and as a result thousands may have been contaminated, many of whom do not know that they carry the virus.

videos.title: An Englishman in Sarajevo
videos.overview: As he completes his controversial mission as commander of the UN protection force in Bosnia, British General Sir Michael Rose gives Panorama a unique insight into the most dangerous military posting in Europe.

videos.title: Gerry Adams - The Man We Hate to Love
videos.overview: This remarkable profile of Gerry Adams shows him in a surprisingly positive light, and asks if the government is doing enough to help him keep IRA hardliners on side.

videos.title: The Million Dollar Spy
videos.overview: In an exclusive interview with Aldrich Ames, allegedly the most damaging traitor in CIA history, Panorama tells the extraordinary story of how he became the world's most highly-paid spy. Reports by Margaret Gilmore.

videos.title: Dead Poor
videos.overview: Average life expectancy in England is 73 for a man and 79 for a woman - but not if you are poor. Panorama looks at new evidence that death rates among Britain's poor are rising for the first time in decades.

videos.title: The Killing Screens
videos.overview: In the week that Oliver Stone's controversial film Natural Born Killers is finally released in Britain, Panorama asks if violent films cause real life violence. Reports by Vivian White.

videos.title: Whose Death Is It Anyway?
videos.overview: Should doctors respect the wishes of the seriously ill who want to die? Panorama investigates whether patients should have the right to tell doctors in advance not to treat them. Do "living wills" represent the ultimate freedom of choice.

videos.title: Pulp Future
videos.overview: Are we facing a future of violence and chaos? In the programme's contribution to Science Week, Panorama looks at the alarming prophecies of post-apocalyptic films such as Mad Max and Blade Runner.

videos.title: Profits on Tap
videos.overview: Tonight's programme poses some tough financial questions for the privatised British water industry. Are its customers footing more than their fair share of the bills? Reports by John Penycate.

videos.title: Home Truths
videos.overview: The slump in the housing market has left more than a million homeowners victims of negative equity. How did it go so wrong, and will your house ever recover its value again? Vivian White reports.

videos.title: The Plane Truth
videos.overview: How safe are Britain's aeroplanes? Why are parts from war wrecks, cars and even bed springs ending up in planes used by airlines all over the world? Panorama investigates the alarming trade in bogus aircraft parts. Jane Corbin reports.

videos.title: The Line of Fire
videos.overview: Two men fire guns in the street. One is in west Yorkshire firing blanks: British police shoot him dead. The other is in New Jersey, USA, with 200 live rounds: American police arrest him unharmed. Gerry Northam reports.

videos.title: Wish I Weren't Here
videos.overview: British citizens who are arrested for alleged crimes in EU countries such as Germany, Spain and Portugal are almost never given bail, and are often not told what's happening to them.

videos.title: Baby Blues
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the desperate plight of one in ten mothers who suffer from postnatal mental illness. New research shows that mothers with postnatal illness are a long-term danger not only to themselves but also to their children.

videos.title: Drug Rule
videos.overview: Murders, machete attacks, shootings and a firebombing have hit a quiet Scottish town - and all because of a sleeping pill. Panorama reports on the crime, violence and fear caused by addiction to Temazepam.

videos.title: Rwanda: The Bloody Tricolour
videos.overview: This Panorama special investigated how the French government was deeply implicated in the Rwandan genocide. It revealed the true extent of French covert military assistance to the Rwandan government between 1990 and 1994.

videos.title: Waiting for Labour
videos.overview: On the day that the Labour Party Conference opens in Brighton, Gavin Hewitt examines what a "new Labour" government could offer Britain - if Tony Blair makes it to number 10.

videos.title: Howard's Way
videos.overview: The Home Secretary, Michael Howard, claims that he is beating crime; in fact, crime recorded by the police has fallen for the 2nd year running. Panorama talks to key players in the criminal justice system, some of who take a different view

videos.title: Men Aren't Working
videos.overview: Panorama reports on the plight of many young men who appear to be losing out to women - at home, at school, at college and, more significantly, in the jobs market. Stephen Bradshaw reports.

videos.title: Panorama Special: The Story of Child B
A Peace Without Honour
videos.overview: In Panorama tonight, Lord Owen tells the story of his years as European negotiator in war-torn Yugoslavia. Speaking candidly about his views on the senior American, Balkan and British figures that he dealt with.

videos.title: Class Struggle
videos.overview: Are Britain's children being let down by bad teachers? The latest research from the government's education inspectorate, Ofsted, suggests that some teachers may not be up to their jobs. Many teachers do not approve of the govt's reforms.

videos.title: An Interview with HRH The Princess of Wales
videos.overview: Diana, Princess of Wales, speaks openly for the first time about her separation from the Prince of Wales in a frank interview for the BBC's Panorama programme.

videos.title: Boozing for Britain
videos.overview: Alcohol abuse is responsible for up to 40,000 deaths every year in Britain, as well as domestic incidents, absenteeism and crime.

videos.title: From Cradle to Grave: Paying for the Future
videos.overview: Tonight, in the first programme of a special two part investigation on the reality of the welfare state, reporter Stephen Bradshaw looks at broken promises. Like families having to sell their parents homes to pay for old age care.

videos.title: From Cradle to Grave: Paying for the Future
videos.overview: The 2nd programme of a two-part investigation into the welfare state. Stephen Bradshaw looks at the implications of the middle classes increasingly looking to private insurance for everything from pensions, schools fees and medical care.

videos.title: Did the NHS Fail?
videos.overview: On 8 December last year, a 10 yr old boy from Stockport, Nicholas Geldard died in a Leeds hospital. In his last hours he was taken to 4 different hospitals; refused an intensive care bed at four others. Did the NHS fail Nicholas Geldard?

videos.title: Empress on the Rocks
videos.overview: The stranding of the Sea Empress oil tanker at the mouth of the Cleddau Estuary off Milford Haven in February 1996 resulted in 72,000 tonnes of crude oil and 370 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, escaping into the sea.

videos.title: War Crime - Five Days in Hell
videos.overview: The Bosnian Serb army stand accused of some of the worst war crimes to be committed since the end of the Second World War. Panorama tells the inside story of what really happened when Srebrenica fell in July 1995.

videos.title: A Ray Of Hope
videos.overview: Gerry Northam presents a programme looking at controversy surrounding perceived results of drugs trials on AZT (marketed as Retrovir) since early 1980's, which have been interpreted by drug companies to show benefits of taking drugs early.

videos.title: High Society?
videos.overview: As part of the week-long series Dealing with Drugs, a look at the increasing use of recreational drugs, not just among the young, but among the professional middle-classes. Is society beginning to adjust and even tolerate the drug culture.

videos.title: Death of a Principle
videos.overview: Last year nearly 200 people were publicly beheaded in Saudi Arabia, yet the British Government does not criticise its closest Middle East ally. John Ware reports on Britain's relationship with the regime.

videos.title: A Life in Limbo
videos.overview: Thomas Creedon was born severely brain-damaged. Unable to see or hear, he was kept alive only through modern medicine. His parents were prepared to take their case to the high court to fight for the right to let their son die.

videos.title: Hard Lessons
videos.overview: Are our children being let down by primary school education? New research suggests that over the last 25 years, standards in maths have fallen noticeably. Vivian White reports on what is going wrong in our primary schools.

videos.title: Mad Cows and Englishmen - The Making of the Beef Crisis
videos.overview: So far BSE has meant the deaths of 160,000 cows and may lead to the condition Creutzfeldt Jakob Disease in humans. As the Government's handling of the "mad cow" crisis threatens to split Europe, Gerry Northam reports.

videos.title: Off the Rails?
videos.overview: In the brave new world of privatised railways, it's cheaper to send trains by road than by rail. New owners of the track charge operators so much that many prefer to load them onto trailers to be sent down the motorway.

videos.title: The Drugs Olympics
videos.overview: Swifter, higher, stronger is the Olympic motto but has the athlete's ultimate dream to win gold created a culture of world-class cheats? Tom Mangold talks to Olympic athletes en route to this year's games who admit to having taken drugs.

videos.title: Dunblane - The Legacy
videos.overview: Panorama begins with this report on the aftermath of the massacre when Thomas Hamilton killed 16 children and their teacher at Dunblane Primary School. Jane Franchi talks to families whose children were murdered in the shooting.

videos.title: Have They Got News for You
videos.overview: The spin doctors politicians rely upon to influence the news have been called "the men in the dark" . Do they help politicians float stories that can later be denied, or simply protect their parties from an obsessed media?

videos.title: The Billion Dollar Man
videos.overview: Sir James Goldsmith is a billionaire at the gate of British politics - a financier who intends spending huge amounts of money promoting the Referendum Party at the next general election. Goldsmith's impact and money is widely feared.

videos.title: On the Trail of the Real Bill Clinton
videos.overview: As America prepares to vote for its next President and the candidates' election campaigns roll towards their conclusion, Edward Stourton journeys across the country on the trail of President Bill Clinton.

videos.title: Violent Women
videos.overview: Statistics show that British women are committing more and more violent crimes. Panorama investigates the shift in the traditional role of women as victims or accessories to crime to the aggressor. Su Pennington reports.

videos.title: Broken Hearts
videos.overview: Martin Bashir reports on what seems to be a widescale ignorance of the easily-treatable Kawasaki disease, the biggest cause of heart disease among children in the western world.

videos.title: Your Pound In Their Pocket: Panorama's Tax Bombshell
videos.overview: Tonight, Peter Jay contrasts political rhetoric of last 20 years with realities of tax burden, to discover if anything has changed.

videos.title: The Price Is Wrong
videos.overview: With Christmas imminent. Panorama investigates allegations that the prices of hi-fi's, televisions and fridges are being kept artificially high. and reporter John Ware explains why finding a bargain might be difficult this year.

videos.title: Medicine's Missing Millions
videos.overview: The NHS is strapped for cash, yet hospital managers and doctors agree that moving some services onto single sites could release huge sums which could be spent on patient care. But there is resistance to closures and other reforms.

videos.title: Drug Crime
videos.overview: The first of a two-part investigation into evidence which suggests there is a revolution in crime fuelled by drug addiction.

videos.title: Crime and Punishment
videos.overview: The second of two special reports, this week asking if tougher prison sentences really cut crime. Gavin Hewitt reports.

videos.title: The Great Euro Debate
videos.overview: Britain will soon have to decide whether to join a single currency in Europe. David Dimbleby invites key commentators, leaders of industry and a studio audience to discuss the questions that may determine the country's future.

videos.title: Missing Mum
videos.overview: Can working women successfully balance their careers and family? New research suggests that children, of working mothers are more likely to suffer from behavioural problems and gain lower exam scores than those whose mothers stay at home.

videos.title: Facing Up to Genocide - Valentina's Story
videos.overview: Updating his 1994 report on the killing of Tutsis in Rwanda, Fergal Keane returns to the country to tell the story of 13-year-old Valentina.

videos.title: The Copper Ring
videos.overview: As Yasuo Hamanaka comes to trial in Tokyo, Michael Robinson investigates the western brokers who made millions from his speculation on the international copper market. In a tale of market manipulation and unfair pricing on a grand scale.

videos.title: Predators
videos.overview: It is the name given to the most dangerous inmates in British prisons today, and psychopaths are generally considered to be untreatable. Panorama examines the minds of these men, and investigates if successful treatment is possible.

videos.title: U-Turn
videos.overview: As Britain's road network reaches saturation point forecasters predict an increase in gridlock, road rage and pollution. New roads designed to ease the pressure on existing routes quickly fill up with traffic.

videos.title: Hear No Evil
videos.overview: Investigation into paedophilia in children's homes in North-West.

videos.title: Abortion: Behind Closed Doors
videos.overview: Although it has been legally available for 30 years, and has become one of the most common operations performed, abortion remains controversial and is often kept secret. Now some campaigners want to make abortion an election issue.

videos.title: The Leader Interview: Tony Blair
videos.overview: The first of four Panorama specials in which David Dimbleby conducts live interviews with the leaders of the three main political parties. Tonight's guest is Tony Blair.

videos.title: The Leader Interview: Dafydd Wigley/Alex Salmond
videos.overview: Tonight's guests are Dafydd Wigley, leader of Plaid Cymru, and Alex Salmond, leader of the Scottish National Party.

videos.title: The Leader Interview: Paddy Ashdown
videos.overview: The third of four programmes in which David Dimbleby conducts live interviews with the leaders of the main political parties. Tonight's guest is the leader of the Liberal Democrats Paddy Ashdown.

videos.title: The Leader Interview: John Major
videos.overview: The last of four programmes putting the leaders of the main political parties under the spotlight. Tonight, David Dimbleby interviews the Prime Minister and Conservative leader, John Major.

videos.title: Water Torture
videos.overview: How water industry makes money.

videos.title: The Terror Network
videos.overview: Investigation into Iranian terrorist network.

videos.title: A Costly Cure?
videos.overview: Potential problems of radiotherapy treatment.

videos.title: Yesterday's Men?
videos.overview: On eve of vote for a new leader, a look back at Major's premiership.

videos.title: Down the Tube
videos.overview: An investigation into the London Underground system reveals 40-year-old trains, signals and tracks that have been patched up since the war, and 100-year-old tunnels that are crumbling.

videos.title: Prescription for Fraud
videos.overview: A National Health Service prescription form is supposed to provide the sick with free medicine, but in the hands of crooked doctors and chemists it has become the key to a multi-million pound fraud.

videos.title: Kill Or Cure
videos.overview: Prescribed by the NHS and distributed by health workers, the drug methadone is designed to help wean addicts off heroin. But it is also a powerful and dangerous narcotic which is linked to the deaths of hundreds of young people every year.

videos.title: The Fall Of Flight 800
videos.overview: An investigation into reason for crash of TWA 800.

videos.title: Migrant Mafia
videos.overview: A report on illegal immigrants smuggled into Britain.

videos.title: The Scottish Parliament
videos.overview: David Dimbleby presents a special live edition of Panorama from Edinburgh on the eve of the historic voting which could give Scotland its own Parliament.

videos.title: Diana - The Last Day
videos.overview: A Mercedes has crashed in a tunnel in Paris. A princess and her companion are dead.

videos.title: Playing with Fire
videos.overview: An investigation into increase in number of young arsonists in Britain.

videos.title: Hard Labour
videos.overview: Government policy on single-parent families.

videos.title: The Ultimate Taboo
videos.overview: Child sexual abuse by women may be more prevalent than people care to admit. Panorama talks to victims, to offenders and to experts who believe it is time to acknowledge the true extent of the problem. Su Pennington reports.

videos.title: Crisis In Care: Safe In Their Hands
videos.overview: Report on controversial NHS care in community program.

videos.title: Crisis In Care: A Risk Worth Taking
videos.overview: In the second of two reports on the Health Service, Panorama highlights problems facing hospitals this winter as a result of increasing waiting lists and an acute shortage of beds.

videos.title: Gay Times
videos.overview: Vivian White reports on changes in political attitudes to issues such as gays in the military and homosexual marriage, parenting and education.

videos.title: The Surrogate
videos.overview: An exclusive report on case of surrogate mother Karen Roche.

videos.title: The British Disease
videos.overview: The presence of new variant CJD in British blood supplies.

videos.title: The People's Monarchy?
videos.overview: A report on Royal Family's plans for future of Monarchy.

videos.title: Myra Hindley
videos.overview: Thirty-one years on, should life still mean life for Myra Hindley?

videos.title: The Greenhouse Wars
videos.overview: The earth's heating up, our weather's becoming more extreme, scientists warn man is to blame. Tonight on Panorama will our leaders seize this chance to save the earth or will they squander it in the greenhouse wars.

videos.title: The Money Game
videos.overview: How football, glory game, has become money game.

videos.title: The Sky's The Limit
videos.overview: A debate over Britain's new Eurofighter aircraft.

videos.title: Bent
videos.overview: Follow-up exposé of corrupt policemen.

videos.title: The Battle of the Green Belt
videos.overview: Housing development in English countryside.

videos.title: The Price of Peace
videos.overview: Britain's nuclear submarine fleet played a vital part in maintaining peace in Europe during the Cold War. But now former submariners and dockyard workers are falling ill with cancer and leukaemia.

videos.title: All the President's Women
videos.overview: Sexual scandal leading to crisis for Clinton's presidency.

videos.title: On the Sick
videos.overview: There are over 2 million adults of working age claiming long-term sickness and disability benefits, a cost of over £14 billion a year to the taxpayer. The government wants to get many of those categorised as sick/disabled into employment.

videos.title: Branson's Pickle
videos.overview: The last government promised that the privatisation of Britain's railways would bring cheaper and more efficient travel. But some of the new rail operators have come under criticism for failing to provide reliable services.

videos.title: Dome!
videos.overview: The Millennium Dome has been called an unforgivable waste of 3/4 of a billion pounds, almost half of which would come from the National Lottery. With less than 2 years to go, the government has still not said what will be inside the Dome.

videos.title: Rural Revolution
videos.overview: The Government has said that uneconomic farms will have to close as subsidies are cut. Last year farm incomes fell by nearly 50 percent, pushing thousands of small farmers to the brink of bankruptcy.

videos.title: Childcare On The Cheap
videos.overview: With the government encouraging more mothers to go out to work, Panorama investigates the quality of care on offer to children of working parents who cannot afford the high fees usually associated with good childcare.

videos.title: Teacher, I Need You
videos.overview: Education specialists and politicians claim there is a crisis in teacher recruitment with the number of applications for teacher-training courses falling and thousands of experienced teachers applying for retirement. Vivian White reports.

videos.title: Special Hospitals
videos.overview: Britain's special hospitals house many of the most dangerous people in society. The patients have committed the most terrible crimes but are themselves mentally ill. Now the future of such hospitals is in question.

videos.title: Nicking the Neighbours
videos.overview: A family with 7 children are evicted from their council home because neighbours claim they made life intolerable. Panorama examines the tough new measures being used by authorities to remove "nuisance neighbours" from housing estates.

videos.title: Settlement or Sell Out?
videos.overview: This week may see the birth of an historic peace agreement in N. Ireland, but will Sinn Fein and the IRA be part of it? Panorama investigates whether Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness are likely to accept or reject the settlement on offer.

videos.title: Health - The Trust Betrayed
videos.overview: As the Government appoints a fraud-buster for the Health Service, Panorama reports on cases involving doctors and opticians where millions of pounds have gone missing or have been falsely claimed.

videos.title: Children Of Crime: The Drugs Debate
videos.overview: Studio debate with Keith Hellawell following new drugs strategy.

videos.title: Defend the Children
videos.overview: Addresses concerns of relatives of victims and locals at paedophiles such as Sidney Cooke being released into their areas.

videos.title: The Diana Dividend
videos.overview: Across the world, unofficial memorabilia of Diana, Princess of Wales is already raking in millions of pounds, but should the official Memorial Fund cash in on her memory, or should it be wound up?

videos.title: The Nurses' Story
videos.overview: Following their return home, the story of two British nurses - Lucille McLauchlan and fellow nurse Deborah Parry. The pair were jailed for the killing of Australian Yvonne Gilford in 1996 in Saudi Arabia.

videos.title: Episode 19
videos.overview: NHS failure to prevent deaths of babies following heart surgery in Bristol.

videos.title: How to Win the World Cup
videos.overview: While fans scrabble around for tickets at inflated prices on the black market, sponsors offer free entry to matches and hospitality. Panorama asks if the fans now matter when it's the money men who will really win at the World Cup.

videos.title: The Louise Woodward Interview
videos.overview: Louise Woodward, British au pair convicted of involuntary manslaughter of a child under her care in Massachusetts, gives her first television interview since returning home to Britain.

videos.title: The Car Cartel
videos.overview: Britain is known as "Treasure Island" to the car industry, because of the large profits to be had from the inflated prices of cars. Panorama investigates what is being called one of the biggest price-fixing rackets in the world.

videos.title: The Spy's Story: The Plot To Kill Gaddafi
videos.overview: Interview with David Shayler, former MI5 officer awaiting extradition from French jail to face charges of breaking Official Secrets Act.

videos.title: The Love Drug
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the impotence drug Viagra, including evidence of abuse and concerns that not enough is known about its human and financial costs.

videos.title: Workaholics
videos.overview: There is a growing army of workaholics choosing to sacrifice time spent with family and friends for extra time at the office. But is the familiar image of stressed employees, forced to work long hours to safeguard their jobs, just a myth?

videos.title: Failing at Four
videos.overview: This school term more 4 year-olds are starting formal classes than ever before. There are doubts about whether school is the right environment for such young children. Could starting too young lead to major problems for a whole generation?

videos.title: The Cruelty Connection
videos.overview: In America, the FBI now believes that serial killers start their pattern of violence with attacks on animals. Politicians are giving the link more credence after a spate of schoolyard shootings by youths with a history of abuse of pets.

videos.title: To Catch a Cop
