videos.overview: Investigation into why Madeleine McCann's parents have found it so hard to shake off the suspicion that they somehow had a role in her disappearance.

videos.title: Please Look After Dad
videos.overview: Investigation into the case of a woman convinced that the powerful anti-psychotic drugs prescribed for her father's dementia were doing him harm, and the disclosure of the results of a long-term scientific study which shows that she may have been right.

videos.title: The Battle for Basra Palace
videos.overview: Using combat footage shot by the soldiers themselves, the story of the last and bloodiest British fight in southern Iraq - the battle for Basra Palace.

videos.title: Basra - The Legacy
videos.overview: Reporter Jane Corbin examines the dark heart of Basra. Once Iraq's most cosmopolitan city, it is now a place where murder and corruption is rife.

videos.title: One Click from Danger
videos.overview: An update to our film 'One Click from Danger' about internet paedophiles exploiting vulnerable youngsters online.

videos.title: Destination UK
videos.overview: Paul Kenyon follows the most dangerous illegal immigration route into Europe, used by tens and thousands of migrants a year seeking a better life, and revisits the survivors whose epic journey ended with them marooned on a tuna net in the middle of the Mediterranean.

videos.title: Britain's Protection Racket
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover to expose the flaws in Britain's seven-billion-pound security industry.

videos.title: Cocaine: Alex James in Colombia
videos.overview: Former cocaine-using Blur bassist Alex James travels to Colombia. He meets the drug farmers, sellers and enforcers, and hears the message that every gram is tainted in blood.

videos.title: Bursting the House Price Bubble
videos.overview: Investigation into sharp practice in the housing market which has kept house prices artificially high and plunged homeowners into negative equity.

videos.title: No More Mandelas
videos.overview: After witnessing the end of apartheid, Fergal Keane returns to South Africa to find out what happened to the hope from that time.

videos.title: Bottled Water - Who Needs It?
videos.overview: Reporter Tom Heap sets out to discover if the popularity of bottled water is merely a triumph of marketing over common sense.

videos.title: On Whose Orders?
videos.overview: Jeremy Vine interviews Tony Blair's Attorney General Lord Goldsmith and General Sir Mike Jackson, asking how rules preventing abuse and torture of prisoners in Iraq were overturned, and analysing new claims that could bring disgrace to the Army.

videos.title: Taking Back The Streets
videos.overview: Richard Bilton examines the dilemma of Garry Newlove, the father beaten to death in the streets. Is a new community action the answer to teenage gangs?

videos.title: Shaken Babies?
videos.overview: Investigates the row behind shaken-baby syndrome. Last year, childminder Keran Henderson was convicted of shaking an 11-month-old baby to death. Her friends and family say she couldn't have done it, despite medical reports suggesting otherwise.

videos.title: Teenage Sex For Sale
videos.overview: Gerry Northam investigates ruthless gangs who are targeting teenage girls and offering drugs and excitement. Within weeks, the children are made to work as prostitutes - having sex with a queue of men. This isn't Eastern European people trafficking but British girls on British streets.

videos.title: Jersey - Island of Secrets
videos.overview: Current affairs programme with Jeremy Vine. It is six weeks since police started their search of Haut de la Garenne children's home on Jersey. Other homes and careworkers now being named by alleged abuse victims and many believe there has been a deliberate cover up.

videos.title: Divide and Rule
videos.overview: Ten years on from the Good Friday Agreement, Panorama examines what power-sharing has done for those living with Northern Ireland's deep sectarian divisions.

videos.title: Feeling the Pinch
videos.overview: Credit crunch, rising fuel prices and talk of recession - we've been warned of a tough year ahead. But how will we really be affected? Declan Curry discovers if we have what it takes to weather the storm of the global forces buffeting our economy.

videos.title: Something in the Air
videos.overview: Pilots almost passing out at the controls; passengers who say they've been made ill by toxic fumes. Can polluted air on board planes damage your health? Panorama carries out its own tests to discover just what's in the air we breathe when we fly.

videos.title: How Clean is Your Hospital?
videos.overview: Sally Magnusson goes inside a trust which lost 90 patients to the superbug c.difficile, which accounts for four times as many deaths as MRSA.

videos.title: Mission Impossible
videos.overview: The UN polices conflicts around the world, but can it police itself? Raphael Rowe reveals how the organisation is struggling to eradicate the rot at its core.

videos.title: Prisons Unlocked
videos.overview: Panorama investigates claims that unsuitable and dangerous convicts are being sent to open prisons to help solve the overcrowding crisis.

videos.title: Tested to Destruction
videos.overview: Current affairs. Are schoolchildren in England given too many exams? Vivian White reports.

videos.title: The Challenge of the 60s
videos.overview: Experts and diplomats including Lord Hurd, Christopher Mallaby and Bernard Lovell assess the predictions made about the world's future in an edition of Panorama from 1960.

videos.title: Britain on the Sick
videos.overview: Current affairs programme presented by Jeremy Vine. Shelley Jofre examines the Government's tough new benefit rules.

videos.title: One Click from Capture
videos.overview: A look at how Panorama's simple experiment of putting a young girl's details onto social networking websites ended with the arrest of an online predator.

videos.title: The Property Game
videos.overview: Vigorous investigation of a topical issue. Richard Bilton meets the winners and losers in the property market. Is the British love affair with home ownership over?

videos.title: What Happened After Taking On the Taliban?
videos.overview: Current affairs. Panorama meets the soldiers featured in last year's Taking On the Taliban special, to find out what they're doing now.

videos.title: Daylight Robbery - What happened to the $23billion?
videos.overview: Jane Corbin investigates the cases which threaten to reveal the corruption behind the past five years of war in the Middle East.

videos.title: Young Gunmen
videos.overview: Current affairs. Panorama investigates the rise of armed teenage street gangs, speaking to former gangsters, the police and the young gunmen themselves.

videos.title: Primark: On the Rack
videos.overview: Panorama puts Primark's claims that it can deliver cheap, fast fashion without breaking ethical guidelines to the test.

videos.title: Taking Back The Streets
videos.overview: Panarama investigates the rise of armed teenage street gangs and discovers how shockingly ingrained the culture of guns and violence is in Britain.

videos.title: NHS for Sale
videos.overview: Sally Magnusson investigates the creeping privatisation of the NHS.

videos.title: China's Secret War
videos.overview: Panorama provides evidence of how China is supplying the Sudanese government with arms to enable it to wage a campaign of violence in Darfur - all for oil.

videos.title: Friends in High Places
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the government's proposals for a third runway at Heathrow which, critics argue, will have a dramatic effect on the environment.

videos.title: Can We Afford to Fill Up?
videos.overview: With the price of fuel rocketing at the pumps, Jane Corbin reports on how fuel prices are affecting Britain and what alternatives might be available.

videos.title: Racing's Dirty Secret
videos.overview: Panorama investigates horse racing and reveals why those running the sport are so concerned about gamblers betting on horses not to win, but to lose.

videos.title: China's Olympic Promise
videos.overview: As the Games approach, award-winning journalist John Sweeney travels across China to discover whether foreign journalists are being allowed to report freely.

videos.title: Notes on a Dirty Island
videos.overview: Travel writer Bill Bryson presents a personal and passionate account of how Britain has become a rubbish tip since his arrival from the USA in 1972.

videos.title: The NHS Postcode Lottery: It Could Be You
videos.overview: Shelley Jofre takes a road trip around the UK and discovers how the quality of treatment from the NHS very much depends on where you live.

videos.title: True Brits
videos.overview: Current affairs with Jeremy Vine. An investigation into how factors such as mass immigration and devolution are forever changing the concept of 'Britishness'.

videos.title: How the Economy Got Personal
videos.overview: Current affairs. Jeremy Vine presents personal stories of regular Britons affected by the credit crunch.

videos.title: Can Money Grow on Trees?
videos.overview: Panorama asks whether the money markets can achieve what campaigners and law enforcement have so far failed to, and make trees more valuable alive than dead.

videos.title: Terror in the Skies?
videos.overview: Peter Taylor uncovers the inside story of the operation which thwarted a terrorist plot to cause explosions and led to increased security at British airports.

videos.title: Omagh: What the Police Were Never Told
videos.overview: Peter Taylor uncovers the inside story of the operation which thwarted a terrorist plot to cause explosions and led to increased security at British airports.

videos.title: How Safe is my Money?
videos.overview: Jane Corbin looks at how the crisis facing the world's financial insitutions could impact on the nation's banks, mortgages, insurance and pensions.

videos.title: You Can Run...
videos.overview: But can you hide? Simon Boazman investigates how much information is held on him, whether it is secure and if he can reduce his data trail.

videos.title: Next Stop, Downing Street?
videos.overview: Nick Robinson accompanies Conservative Party leader David Cameron to Birmingham as he attempts to persuade voters he is prime minister material.

videos.title: The Secret Policeman Returns
videos.overview: In the wake of the resignation of Britain's top police officer, Panorama investigates racism in Britain's police force. Mark Daly - who exposed racism amongst police recruits in The Secret Policeman five years ago - returns to uncover the truth about being a Black Ethnic Minority Cop today.

videos.title: Should We Be Scared of Russia?
videos.overview: Mark Franchetti meets Vladimir Putin's inner circle in an attempt to decipher Russia's intentions on domestic and international fronts.

videos.title: Obama and the Pitbull: An American Tale
videos.overview: Matt Frei investigates Barack Obama's rise in the opinion polls, and asks if the current financial crisis has put him on the home straight.

videos.title: Britain in the Red - Your Questions Answered
videos.overview: Jeremy Vine asks why our economy ran into trouble, and who is to blame for the credit crunch and banking crisis which threatens to affect us all.

videos.title: Three Bloody Summers
videos.overview: The British Commander on the ground admits the war against the Taliban cannot be won by force alone in this eye-opening assessment of the Afghanistan conflict.

videos.title: Can't Pay, Won't Pay
videos.overview: With the credit crunch affecting everyone, Panorama reveals the lengths some lenders are now going to in order to get borrowers to pay off their debts.

videos.title: What Happened to Baby P?
videos.overview: A six-month investigation by the programme reveals the mistakes and missed opportunities that led to the death of a 17-month-old boy known only as Baby P.

videos.title: Addicted to Aid
videos.overview: Reporter Sorious Samura visits Uganda and his home country of Sierra Leone to reveal how aid money is lost, stolen and frittered away.

videos.title: Comeback Coal
videos.overview: An investigation into the Government's support of a new wave of opencast coal mining, in spite of fierce opposition from local communities.

videos.title: Shannon: The Mother of All Lies
videos.overview: Panorama presents the inside story on the disappearance of Shannon Matthews, as it investigates the events that led to Karen Matthews being convicted for the kidnap of her own daughter.

videos.title: I'll Die When I Choose
videos.overview: Politician and Parkinson's sufferer Margo MacDonald uncovers the truth about assisted dying, meeting those with illnesses like hers who are desperate to die.

videos.title: Britain's Terror Heartland
videos.overview: Jane Corbin makes the hazardous journey to the frontline in the War on Terror, the remote and forbidding mountains along the Pakistan-Afghan border.

videos.title: The Year Britain's Bubble Burst
videos.overview:
It has been a cataclysmic year for our banks and economy, and a year in which the role of the BBC's Business Editor has been in the spotlight as never before.

With exclusive interviews with the major players, Robert Peston reflects on how these momentous events will affect us all.

videos.title: Kids Behaving Badly
videos.overview:
Whether it is 10-year-olds talking about who they have snogged or schoolgirls calling themselves sluts on their social-networking profile pages, it seems our kids can't get away from sex. But what happens when the banter and name-calling gets physical?

Jeremy Vine reveals the problem of sexual bullying in our schools and hears from experts, parents and teachers - but most importantly from the kids themselves - on what we can do to tackle it.

videos.title: Jailed for a Knife
videos.overview: Raphael Rowe goes inside prisons to gain rare access to the young offenders convicted of carrying, using or even killing with a knife.

videos.title: What Now, Mr President?
videos.overview: Barack Obama takes over as US President with a promise to change America and make it a fairer place. Can he reshape the world's most powerful country?

videos.title: Have I Got Bad Language For You?
videos.overview: Frank Skinner sets out to discover if the Ross-Brand storm really was a watershed in broadcasting's debate about bad language and offence.

videos.title: Tax Me if You Can
videos.overview: Britain is bust and ordinary taxpayers are getting hammered, but it seems that the super-rich can still squirrel their money away in tax havens like Liechtenstein, Jersey and the Caymans.  John Sweeney follows the missing millions, and asks if it is time to close the tax havens down.

videos.title: Gaza: Out of the Ruins
videos.overview: As Israel prepares to vote on its future, Jeremy Bowen travels through a devastated Gaza to ask where the recent conflict now leaves the future of the region.

videos.title: Muslim First, British Second
videos.overview: The current affairs series asks how radicals should be treated and examines suspicions that community projects are being used to gather intelligence.

videos.title: Credit Where It's Due
videos.overview: Business dragon Theo Paphitis asks if the banks and the government are doing enough to help Britain's 4.7 million small businesses survive the recession.

videos.title: What Happens After Sorry?
videos.overview: As RBS announces what are predicted to be the biggest losses in British history, Panorama tells the story of the bank's dramatic fall from grace.

videos.title: Immigration - Time for an Amnesty?
videos.overview: Panorama looks at a proposed amnesty for hundreds of thousands of long-standing illegal immigrants, championed by London mayor Boris Johnson.

videos.title: Crime Pays
videos.overview: Panorama reveals how organised crime is defeating attempts to claw back its profits, and how the Crown has been reduced to making tax deals with criminals.

videos.title: Who Will Save the Savers?
videos.overview: As the credit crunch pushes Britain's pensions and savings time-bomb to a new level, Panorama asks experts to help those facing an uncertain future.

videos.title: 1959: A Panorama Guide
videos.overview: Documentary looking back at 1959 through the eyes of the BBC current affairs programme Panorama, recalling a time when Britain finally realised that the old world was disappearing.

videos.title: The Gunmen Who Never Went Away
videos.overview: With soldiers and police once again being killed in the province, Panorama offers a detailed analysis of the resurgent terrorist threat in Northern Ireland, based on ten years' work investigating the breakaway Republican movement, its aims, its roots and its tactics.

videos.title: Slumdogs and Millionaires
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover in the millionaires' playground of Dubai to look at luxury developments. Reporter Ben Anderson discovers that behind the glossy sales brochures is an army of construction workers living in appalling conditions.

videos.title: Britain's Homecare Scandal
videos.overview: Paul Kenyon investigates care of the elderly and goes undercover to expose a world of chaos. Carers on minimum wages - often with little training - battle to provide decent care.

videos.title: Life After Woolies
videos.overview: Current affairs. Since the closure of Woolworths' 807 retail outlets, Panorama has followed some of the 27,000 former staff as they try to escape unemployment.

videos.title: May Contain Nuts
videos.overview: Current affairs. Panorama investigates why the deadly serious matter of health and safety has become a laughing stock, and why it has strayed from its original aim.

videos.title: Who'd Be an NHS Whistleblower?
videos.overview: Margaret Haywood put her career on the line to expose failings in the care of the elderly. Jeremy Vine asks why more aren't willing to speak out.

videos.title: Baby P - The Whole Truth?
videos.overview: Reporter Alison Holt has further revelations on the case of Baby P, the baby boy who died while under the care of social workers in Haringey, London.

videos.title: The Six Billion Dollar Man
videos.overview: John Sweeney goes on the trail of the dark side of banker Sir Allen Stanford who bowled over cricket and is accused of a multi-billion dollar fraud.

videos.title: Stem Cells and Miracles
videos.overview: The current affairs programme follows a British family to China as they pin their hopes on a new stem cell therapy to give their daughter sight.  As evidence mounts that some treatments offered abroad are bogus, will the child's eyesight improve, or are they destined for disappointment?

videos.title: Is Your MP Working for You?
videos.overview: The expenses scandal is just the beginning and not the end of Westminster's troubles. Shelley Jofre reports on the other ways in which the new appetite for transparency may embarrass honourable members.

videos.title: 'A Very Dangerous Doctor'
videos.overview: Vivian White challenges David Southall to answer his critics and uncovers evidence that may support his claim of victimisation.

videos.title: Obama and the Ayatollah
videos.overview: As Iranians prepare to elect a president, Jane Corbin asks whether Obama's recent plea for greater understanding will be heeded.

videos.title: The Death of Kiss and Tell
videos.overview: Investigating the growing trend of celebrities and public figures turning to privacy laws to suppress stories and photographs showing them in a bad light.

videos.title: The Battle of Swat Valley
videos.overview: Exclusive access to airborne troops and to footage shot in Taliban-controlled towns reveal the story of Pakistan's fight against extremists.

videos.title: Will the Scots Ever Be Happy?
videos.overview: Ten years after devolution, the Scots want more power north of the border, and the SNP want a referendum on independence. Can the UK be preserved?

videos.title: What Ever Happened to People Power?
videos.overview: Panorama asks if police tactics aimed at preventing troublemakers taking over demonstrations are eroding the freedom to protest.

videos.title: Licence to Torture
videos.overview: Current affairs. Did interrogation techniques used by the Bush administration after 9/11 break US and international law? Hilary Andersson investigates.

videos.title: Save Our Steel
videos.overview: Current affairs. Panorama helps citizen journalists Steven, Belinda and Tony find out the future of the steel industry, which employs tens of thousands of people.

videos.title: The Trauma Industry
videos.overview: Veteran BBC war reporter Allan Little investigates how the battlefield trauma of the Vietnam War - post-traumatic stress disorder - now ends up in British motor insurance claims, workplace accidents and school bullying.

videos.title: Smugglers' Tales
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the endless game of cat and mouse between prisoners determined to get their fix and officers equally determined to keep drugs out of their jails.

videos.title: The Truth About Happy Hour
videos.overview: Panorama visits the town tackling binge drinking with a radical new approach.  Richard Bilton looks at reclaiming Britain's town centres from the drunk and violent, with the bar that makes it too difficult to get drunk and the battle against cheap drink promotions.

videos.title: What Are We Fighting For?
videos.overview: With British soldiers dying in record numbers and the country arguing over the wisdom of the war, Jane Corbin travels across Afghanistan to ask if the British presence has made the lives of Afghan women any better, which was one of the justifications for going to war in the first place.

videos.title: Gimme Shelter
videos.overview: Panorama reports on the elderly people who are taking to the streets in protest, and threatening legal action, because their residential wardens are being taken away.

videos.title: Britain's Dirty Beaches
videos.overview: Sand, sea and sewage. With the quality of bathing water on the UK's beaches in decline, Panorama investigates the outflow pipes that discharge sewage, tampons and condoms after heavy rain, and commissions its own scientific tests, with some disturbing results.  Declan Lawn reports.

videos.title: Europe or Die Trying
videos.overview: Paul Kenyon travels three thousand miles along the most dangerous illegal immigration route out of Africa. Many die crossing the Sahara, or at sea on the way to a better life in Europe, but can the survivors convince those who follow that Europe in recession is no longer worth the risk?

videos.title: Swine Flu: Everything You Need To Know
videos.overview:
Everything you need to know about the first flu pandemic of the 21st century.

Jeremy Vine, Sophie Raworth and Fergus Walsh travel through the UK and the world to expose the myths and the dangers of swine flu. Who is most vulnerable? How do you avoid it? And can the NHS cope?

videos.title: Banks Behaving Badly?
videos.overview: Billions of taxpayers' money has been handed out to keep the banking system afloat, but what exactly have the banks given customers in return?

videos.title: The Truth About Spending Cuts
videos.overview: The real effects of the recession may just be starting as John Ware challenges the politicians to come clean about their plans to slash public spending.

videos.title: Dying to Be Treated?
videos.overview: In a Panorama special, the programme investigates a key Labour health policy that used the private sector to slash NHS waiting lists. Six years on, was it worth the price?

videos.title: Migrants, Go Home!
videos.overview: Reporter Paul Kenyon continues his journey out of Africa following the route taken by 40,000 migrants a year seeking a better life in Europe.

videos.title: Why Hate Ryanair?
videos.overview:
Vivian White investigates the reasons why the ultimate 'no frills' airline has gained a reputation as the brand Britain loves to hate but can't stop using.

Passengers, suppliers and insiders contribute, and chief executive Michael O'Leary doorsteps the programme makers in his own unique style.

videos.title: Undercover - Hate on the Doorstep
videos.overview: Two British Asian reporters pose as a couple living on a housing estate to investigate racism in Britain. Contains racially offensive language.

videos.title: Freed to Offend Again
videos.overview: Are we safe from dangerous prisoners released back onto our streets? A Panorama investigation reveals the extent of crimes committed by ex-convicts.

videos.title: The Child Protectors
videos.overview: With exclusive access to Coventry's social workers, Panorama follows the emergency response team as they attempt to identify children at risk.

videos.title: Assault on Justice
videos.overview: Shelley Jofre investigates whether punishing violent crimes with cautions and fines is letting some serious criminals off the hook and denying justice to victims.

videos.title: Swimming with Loan Sharks
videos.overview: Loan sharks are thriving in recession-hit Britain, as the poor and vulnerable run out of credit and find themselves relying on criminals instead.  Reporter Simon Boazman finds the victims who have suffered brutal violence, and looks at the lenders who can charge 17,000 per cent interest.

videos.title: Lethal Enterprise
videos.overview: Panorama investigates a little-known law called joint enterprise, used to curb gang violence, and asks if the catch-all policy leads to miscarriages of justice.

videos.title: Can Tesco Save the World?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates whether supermarket giant Tesco is now leading the business fightback against man-made global warming.

videos.title: Can You Forgive Your MP?
videos.overview: Old politics were due to be swept away on a tide of moats and mortgages. But what has changed? Politicians discuss how they can regain the trust of voters.

videos.title: Can't Deliver, Won't Deliver
videos.overview: What is wrong with the Royal Mail? Panorama investigates the service that gets around 5,000 complaints a day, and asks if it is failing its customers.

videos.title: The MP and the Whistleblower
videos.overview: The series takes a look at Iris Robinson, the Member of Parliament at the centre of a current political storm.

videos.title: A Walk in the Park
videos.overview: Jane Corbin walks through the disputed streets and parks of Jerusalem and goes underground to explore tunnels excavated deep below the biblical sites.

videos.title: What's Really in Our Kids' Food?
videos.overview: Shelley Jofre investigates the food being dished up to pre-schoolers at nurseries and at home, and looks at the marketing claims of leading brands.

videos.title: I Helped My Daughter Die
videos.overview: Jeremy Vine talks exclusively to Kay Gilderdale about the night she helped her bedridden daughter kill herself, exploring whether the law should be changed.

videos.title: Are You a Danger to Kids?
videos.overview: Panorama exposes the myths and realities of the new child protection register, and asks whether the new system will actually work.

videos.title: Why Do You Hate Me?
videos.overview: Wheelchair user Simon Green secretly films what it is like to endure disability hate crime, and reveals that many such incidents are not properly prosecuted.

videos.title: Dying for a Biscuit
videos.overview: Reporter Raphael Rowe journeys into the rainforest of Borneo, where he uncovers evidence of palm oil companies developing plantations on protected land.

videos.title: More Than Just a Game
videos.overview: As Africa gears up to host its first football World Cup, Panorama asks if the beautiful game can save a generation fighting to survive in South Africa.

videos.title: Trust Us, We're an NHS Hospital
videos.overview: Panorama investigates how many hospitals may be failing the public while being allowed to assess themselves as good. Simon Boazman reports.

videos.title: Are the Net Police Coming for You?
videos.overview: A proposed new law is threatening to disconnect the millions of internet users who unlawfully download free music, films and TV. Jo Whiley looks at how broadband use at home may never be the same, and could even be cut off.

videos.title: Chocolate - The Bitter Truth
videos.overview: Paul Kenyon goes undercover as a cocoa trader in West Africa and discovers children as young as seven working long hours on cocoa farms, helping to make our chocolate.

videos.title: Passports to Kill
videos.overview: Reporter Jane Corbin shows how British passports and stolen identities were used in the murder of senior Hamas military commander Mahmoud al-Mabhouh in Dubai.

videos.title: Spoilt Rotten?
videos.overview: With unprecedented access to Alder Hey Children's Hospital in Liverpool, Panorama meets the children suffering from preventable conditions as a result of their lifestyles.

videos.title: Is Britain Full?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates overcrowding in the UK. Some argue that the extra population will boost the economy, but will it? What can politicians do to stop the growth?

videos.title: Return of the Real Apprentices
videos.overview: Panorama follows the fortunes of four young people searching for work in Swindon, and discovers how they have responded to the challenge of recession.

videos.title: The Cuts - Can You Fight Back?
videos.overview: Reporter Shelley Jofre looks at the fight to save frontline services as councils across the country tighten their budgets.

videos.title: A Very British Hero
videos.overview: Christina Schmid reveals how the Army is failing in its duty of care to a tiny elite band of soldiers who are at the very forefront of the war in Afghanistan.

videos.title: The Cumbrian Shootings
videos.overview: Panorama's Richard Bilton reports on the events of Wednesday 2nd June, when Derrick Bird switched from quiet cabbie to gun toting psychopath.

videos.title: Man United - Into the Red
videos.overview: Ahead of a possible bid for debt-ridden Manchester United, reporter John Sweeney explores the battle for the soul of the club, and the scale of its debts.

videos.title: BP - In Deep Water
videos.overview: Hilary Andersson examines the full consequences of the explosion on BP's Deepwater Horizon oil rig in the Gulf of Mexico, asking what went wrong and who is really to blame.

videos.title: What's Up with the Weather?
videos.overview: Increasing numbers of us simply don't believe in global warming. Tom Heap speaks to some of the world's leading scientists on both sides of the argument.

videos.title: Can I Sack Teacher?
videos.overview: New research shows that the standard of teaching is the most important factor to a child's education. So why are so many bad teachers being allowed to teach?

videos.title: Orphans of Haiti
videos.overview: Six months after a devastating earthquake struck Haiti, Raphael Rowe returns to uncover what has happened to the country's orphaned and abandoned children.

videos.title: How to Beat the Banks
videos.overview: Reporter Adam Shaw investigates the state of Britain's banks, and reveals that while base rates remain low, the cost of borrowing has risen significantly.

videos.title: It Shouldn't Happen at a Vets'
videos.overview: Filming undercover in one of Britain's largest veterinary chains, Panorama reveals evidence of questionable bills, animals poorly treated, and an unrepentant vet struck off for dishonesty.  Pet owners who take best practice on trust are in for a shock.

videos.title: Generation Game
videos.overview: Current affairs series. Dame Joan Bakewell looks at some of the innovative ways Britain's baby boomers are looking to future-proof their old age.

videos.title: Britain's Unwanted Pets
videos.overview: 2009 saw a big increase in the numbers of stray dogs recorded as being picked up in the UK. Tom Heap goes to Battersea Dogs Home to find out why.

videos.title: Wills - The Final Rip Off?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates companies who make a good living from writing your Last Will and Testament, and exposes the shocking financial pitfalls that face unwary consumers. Is it time for this industry to be properly regulated by law?

videos.title: Death in the Med
videos.overview: As controversy over Israel's blockade of Gaza still rages, Jane Corbin asks what really happened on the Mavi Marmara, when Israeli commandos seized the ship.

videos.title: Please Don't Take Our Child
videos.overview: Darragh MacIntyre reports on the case of an ordinary couple and their extraordinary fight to open up the world of the family courts.

videos.title: Britain's Disappearing Wildlife
videos.overview: A look at the decline of UK wildlife. There is more at stake than simply protecting the beauty of nature - our food supply could be under threat.

videos.title: A Risk Worth Taking?
videos.overview: Shelley Jofre investigates the drug Avandia and asks whether the medicine's regulator is putting the interests of the drugs industry before patients.

videos.title: What the Pope Knew
videos.overview: On the eve of the first Papal visit to Britain in 28 years, Fergal Keane investigates the Pope's personal track record of dealing with paedophile priests.

videos.title: Because We're Worth It - the Taxpayers' Rich List
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the results of the most thorough and extensive investigation ever conducted into public sector pay.

videos.title: Britain in the Dock
videos.overview: Paul Kenyon asks if the British Army can be trusted to police itself, as it stands accused in two separate inquiries of committing war crimes in Iraq.

videos.title: The Secrets of Scientology
videos.overview: Reporter John Sweeney's last investigation into the Church of Scientology resulted in an explosive confrontation with church officials. This time, in a Panorama Special, one of those officials has turned whistleblower to help him reveal the dark secrets of the church, which boasts Hollywood A-listers Tom Cruise and John Travolta among its devotees.

videos.title: Who Took My Pension?
videos.overview: Topical investigation with Jeremy Vine. Penny Haslam reveals the fees and commissions that take vast amounts from our pension pots.

videos.title: Kids in Care
videos.overview: A special report into the quality of state care, spending six months following children in the care of Coventry Social Services to find out if the state can be a real parent.

videos.title: Lord Ashcroft's Millions
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the financial dealings of political donor Lord Ashcroft, who resigned as deputy chairman of the Conservative Party in September 2010.

videos.title: Trapped - The Chile Miners' Story
videos.overview: Reporter Dan McDougall reveals new evidence of massive safety problems in the Chilean mine being ignored just weeks before the collapse.

videos.title: The Great Housing Rip Off?
videos.overview: John Sweeney investigates the so-called 'rogue landlords', housing barons accused of receiving large housing benefits while exploiting the vulnerable.

videos.title: What Have the Drugs Done to Dad?
videos.overview: As the government cracks down on the use of certain drugs, Vivian White reports on the crisis of care in the treatment of patients with dementia.

videos.title: Are You Paying Too Much Tax?
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the situation inside HM Revenue and Customs following the recent tax code realignment.

videos.title: Tax the Fat
videos.overview: With Britain now the fattest nation in Europe, reporter Shelley Jofre investigates the idea of a tax on junk food, travelling to Denmark where it has already been implemented.

videos.title: British Schools, Islamic Rules
videos.overview: Investigation showing that some Muslim children are exposed to extremist preachers and fundamentalist Islamic groups. Also, the part-time schools where hate is on the curriculum.

videos.title: Fifa's Dirty Secrets
videos.overview: Panorama investigates corruption allegations against some of the Fifa officials who will vote on England's World Cup bid, and Andrew Jennings exposes new evidence of bribery.

videos.title: Addicted to Games?
videos.overview: Panorama hears from youngsters who describe their obsessive playing of video games as an addiction, and reporter Raphael Rowe meets leading experts calling for more research.

videos.title: Baby P: In His Mother's Words
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the controversial video-taped interview with the mother of Baby P and asks whether crucial warning signs were missed.

videos.title: Carry On Banking!
videos.overview: As Christmas approaches and Britain's bankers prepare to receive their annual bonuses, Panorama asks if anything has changed since the financial crisis of two years ago.

videos.title: Supermarkets: What Price Cheap Food?
videos.overview: In a Panorama Special, Paul Kenyon looks behind the special offers to examine the true cost of Britain's cheap food, visiting the mega-farms coming our way from the US.

videos.title: Too Much Too Young
videos.overview: Provocative clothing, raunchy dancing on prime-time TV, access to pornography - Panorama examines the growing concern about the sexualisation of children in the UK. Sophie Raworth, a mother of three, goes behind the headlines to discover what images young people are being exposed to, and asks what impact the sexualised world is having on our children. Is too much, too young, putting them at risk?

videos.title: Britain's Missing Dads
videos.overview: Are actively involved dads becoming an endangered species in some parts of Britain? Reporter Declan Lawn investigates what can be done to keep them in the picture.

videos.title: Stop Stalking Me
videos.overview: With stalking affecting an estimated two million people in Britain each year, Panorama tells the extraordinary story of a woman who has been recording years of abuse.

videos.title: The Battle for Bomb Alley
videos.overview: Ben Anderson follows the US Marines who have patrolled the Sangin district of Afghanistan since the British withdrawal last year. Has progress been made?

videos.title: The Battle for Egypt
videos.overview: For the last 14 days, the world has watched a popular uprising against the 30-year-old regime of President Mubarak. Jane Corbin has been filming inside these extraordinary scenes.

videos.title: Forgotten Heroes
videos.overview: Colonel Tim Collins meets the soldiers who return home only to find that their service for Queen and country counts for little on civvy street.

videos.title: WikiLeaks: The Secret Story
videos.overview: John Sweeney assesses what WikiLeaks and its exposing of sensitive official material has achieved and asks whether it has lived up to its own ideals on openness.

videos.title: How to Blow a Fortune
videos.overview: Fergal Keane tries to find out how Ireland got to the brink of bankruptcy after being one of the richest countries in the world. Has bailing them out put the UK economy at risk?

videos.title: Classroom Warriors
videos.overview: Panorama goes back to school to examine government plans to send in the troops to Britain's troubled classrooms. Can they help restore discipline, leadership and respect?

videos.title: Smoking and the Bandits
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the world of the criminal tobacco trade. Sam Poling reveals that more than half of all hand-rolled tobacco in the country is now counterfeit or smuggled.

videos.title: Tabloid Hacks Exposed
videos.overview: Another report from the weekly current affairs programme. Panorama exposes the full extent of the "dark arts" employed by journalists across the industry to get their story.

videos.title: Fighting Gaddafi
videos.overview: The real story of Libya's revolution. How a group of young professionals bravely stood up to the 42-year-long dictatorship. And Paul Kenyon tracks down Gaddafi's son Saadi.

videos.title: My Big Fat Fake Wedding
videos.overview: In this Panorama Special, reporter Richard Bilton goes undercover as a wedding photographer to exposes the lucrative - and growing - world of fake marriages.

videos.title: The Big Squeeze
videos.overview: With the cost of living rising fast and wages falling behind, Panorama unveils new research which shows that most of us are significantly poorer than we were two years ago.

videos.title: Finished at Fifty?
videos.overview: With more long-term unemployed over-50s than any other age bracket, Fiona Phillips reveals a group of people facing rejection letters and money worries after a lifetime at work.

videos.title: Living with the Ayatollah
videos.overview: Reporter Jane Corbin asks how much longer Iran can keep a lid on internal unrest as revolution and regime change sweep across the Middle East.

videos.title: The Trillion Dollar Con-Man
videos.overview: Panorama tracks down a fraudster who stole a football club and broke a bank, and asked how one man managed to run rings around the regulators and authorities.

videos.title: Council Houses: Cheats and Victims
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the stories of families who struggle to get by in overcrowded or hazardous homes, or who have no option but to rent properties they simply cannot afford.

videos.title: The Death of Bin Laden
videos.overview: The story of how America tracked down and killed Osama Bin Laden. Featuring interviews with eyewitnesses, victims of Al Qaeda's terror and military and intelligence insiders.

videos.title: Track My Trash
videos.overview: Using tracking equipment inside broken TV sets, Panorama investigates the illegal market in electronic waste - and recycling companies whose credentials may not be all they claim.

videos.title: Fifa: Football's Shame?
videos.overview: With the Fifa presidential elections taking place on 1 June 2011, reporter Andrew Jennings examines whether either candidate is suitable for the role.

videos.title: Undercover Care: The Abuse Exposed
videos.overview: In a special edition of Panorama, Paul Kenyon exposes the truth about a gang of carers out of control, and learns how the care system ignored all the warning signs.

videos.title: A Job to Get Work
videos.overview: Panorama visits Rhyl in North Wales where, in some parts of the town, nearly half of the population are on benefits. The programme hears the stories of some of the unemployed.

videos.title: Can You Trust Your Bank?
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover to test whether staff in Britain's banks have learnt the lessons from the massive penalties imposed for mis-selling insurance and investment products.

videos.title: Breaking into Britain
videos.overview: Evan Davis uncovers the truth behind the economic migrants who cross continents to try to illegally enter Britain, as two reporters follow the dangerous routes they use to get in.

videos.title: Land of Anarchy
videos.overview: Peter Greste finds out what it is like to live amid the anarchy of Somalia, going where no western journalist has been to witness a crisis that threatens millions of lives.

videos.title: Surgery's Dirty Secrets
videos.overview: Sam Poling investigates claims that surgical instruments with dangerous defects are being used in the NHS, and asks if goods are being sourced ethically to protect patient health.

videos.title: Why Hate Junk Mail?
videos.overview: Tom Heap investigates whether Royal Mail would be able to survive without junk mail, and asks what the postal service has to do with the dark side of letters - scam mail.

videos.title: The Great Car Insurance Swindle
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the car insurance industry from top to bottom and infiltrates a criminal gang faking accidents for fraudulent insurance claims. Declan Lawn reports.

videos.title: Murdoch: Breaking the Spell?
videos.overview: For decades, Rupert Murdoch has held a unique position of power in Britain through his media empire. After the revelations of the News of the World phone hacking scandal, Panorama tells the inside story of how the media giant's influence was dramatically challenged.

videos.title: One Born Every 40 Seconds
videos.overview: In the middle of a baby boom, Shelley Jofre reveals that some parts of the UK are facing a shortage of midwives, and asks if the NHS is providing appropriate maternity care.

videos.title: Dying for a Drink
videos.overview: Panorama uncovers the impact alcohol is having on a younger generation of problem drinkers, and asks whether the government is doing enough to stop us drinking ourselves to death.

videos.title: Mugabe's Blood Diamonds
videos.overview: Panorama goes deep into Zimbabwe's Marange diamond fields and uncovers evidence of torture camps and wide scale killings. Will Robert Mugabe face prosecution for these crimes?

videos.title: The August Riots
videos.overview: The worst civil unrest for decades has led to tens of millions of pounds of damage. Panorama tells the story of the August riots and asks what has led a generation to violence.

videos.title: Gerry and the GPs
videos.overview: In this special edition of Panorama, troubleshooter and businessman Sir Gerry Robinson examines the government's plans for the biggest shake-up of the NHS in its history.

videos.title: Tsunami: The Survivors' Stories
videos.overview: Six months on from one of the world's most devastating tsunamis, Panorama's Paul Kenyon returns to Japan to hear remarkable tales of survival amid the epic destruction.

videos.title: Drinking Our Rivers Dry?
videos.overview: As concerns rise over Britain's water supply, Simon Boazman investigates whether the water industry and its regulators are doing enough to protect the nation's rivers.

videos.title: Syria: Inside the Secret Revolution
videos.overview: Will Syria be the next Arab dictatorship to fall? The full story of those struggling against Syria's President Assad, and the truth on his brutal crackdown against his own people.

videos.title: All Work and Low Pay
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover to reveal how some employers exploit loopholes or get round the rules so that their workers are paid below the National Minimum Wage.

videos.title: BNP: The Fraud Exposed
videos.overview: Nick Griffin's British National Party, already under investigation for breaches of electoral law, is facing fresh allegations of corruption. Panorama uncovers new evidence.

videos.title: The Great Fuel Robbery
videos.overview: With exclusive access to the police and HM Revenue and Customs teams tasked with fighting fuel crime, Samantha Poling investigates the multi-million pound black market in fuel.

videos.title: Britain's Child Beggars
videos.overview: Reporter John Sweeney uncovers the truth behind the children begging on Britain's streets, and tracks down the begging gangs to luxury homes in Romania.

videos.title: Britain, Gaddafi and the Torture Trail
videos.overview: Reporter Paul Kenyon presents shocking pictures and testimony, never seen before, that reveal the truth about Colonel Gaddafi's regime and its ties with the British government.

videos.title: Dale Farm: The Big Eviction
videos.overview: Panorama received exclusive access to the families of the Dale Farm travellers, their neighbours and the authorities, prior to and during Britain's biggest ever traveller eviction.

videos.title: Cops Behaving Badly
videos.overview: What happens when the police fail in their duty to protect life, when they get it wrong or when police officers break the law? Richard Bilton investigates cops who behave badly.

videos.title: Britain on the Fiddle
videos.overview: Richard Bilton uses undercover cameras to expose benefit fraudsters sailing yachts and driving Bentleys. Plus the rising tide of benefit cheats using fake identities.

videos.title: What's Fuelling Your Energy Bill?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the inconvenient truth behind the UK's rocketing energy bills - that government policy is stoking much of the rise.

videos.title: Manchester: Inside the Riots
videos.overview: Panorama goes behind the lines with Manchester's police and into the interview rooms with the rioters to tell the story of one of the cities most affected by the August riots.

videos.title: Meet the Burglars
videos.overview: Panorama reporter Raphael Rowe goes into a jail to witness a tense encounter between two young women and the youth who broke into their home while they slept.

videos.title: Who's Getting Rich on your Money?
videos.overview: John Ware investigates the Private Finance Initiative and uncovers evidence of how government claims that PFI gives taxpayers value for money have been manipulated.

videos.title: From Russia With Love
videos.overview: How did an MP's former assistant come to be wrongly accused by MI5 of being a threat to British national security? Katia Zatuliveter speaks exclusively to Peter Taylor.

videos.title: The Truth About Supermarket Price Wars
videos.overview: Sophie Raworth takes her trolley round the aisles of Britain's biggest supermarket chains and reveals some nasty surprises at the checkout.

videos.title: How to Survive the Meltdown
videos.overview: The world economy is in meltdown, the euro is in turmoil and the future looks bleak. Does it have to be so bad? Panorama investigates how Britain plc could survive the crisis.

videos.title: The Truth About Adoption
videos.overview: Adoption is now high on the political agenda as the best option for the 65,000 children in care. This film addresses the hidden cost of adoption breakdown.

videos.title: Stephen Lawrence: Time For Justice
videos.overview: On verdict day of one of the most eagerly awaited trials in recent history, this Panorama Special on the Stephen Lawrence case reveals the untold story of the murder that changed Britain.  For more than a year, reporter Mark Daly and the Panorama team have exclusively followed Stephen's mother Doreen Lawrence as her 18-year fight for justice for her murdered son neared its conclusion.  This moving film charts the history of this iconic case through the eyes of a grieving mother, and reports the inside account of the trial of the two men accused of the black teenager's killing.

videos.title: Train Fares: Taken for a Ride?
videos.overview: Packed in like sardines, on trains that often arrive late... But it is the price of the tickets that really upsets lots of rail travellers, and fares have just gone up to record levels. So why are train fares so expensive? Panorama investigates the cost of riding on the railway.

videos.title: Secrets of the Tory Billionaire
videos.overview: Panorama investigates Lord Ashcroft's links to a controversial construction company in the Caribbean which has gone bust.

videos.title: Hunting the Internet Bullies
videos.overview: Current affairs. With online bullying rapidly growing in size and intensity, Declan Lawn meets X Factor star Cher Lloyd, who describes how cyber attacks are ruining her life.

videos.title: Poor America
videos.overview: With one and a half million American children now homeless, reporter Hilary Andersson meets the school pupils who go hungry in the richest country on Earth.

videos.title: Britain's Hidden Alcoholics
videos.overview: Alastair Campbell meets some of the increasing number of Britain's middle-class professionals for whom one glass of wine after work is never enough.

videos.title: The Cost of Raising Britain
videos.overview: With nurseries and childminders costing families up to a third of their income, and working mums feeling squeezed out of the workplace, Panorama investigates the cost of childcare.

videos.title: The Money Farmers
videos.overview: Samantha Poling reveals how millions of pounds of public money are being paid out to businessmen and millionaire farmers in an abuse of the farming subsidy system.

videos.title: Homs: Journey into Hell
videos.overview: Paul Wood charts the rise and brutal suppression of the uprising in the Syrian city of Homs. What started with hope of revolution now sees refugees fleeing to escape retribution.

videos.title: Britain's Crimes of Honour
videos.overview: Panorama reveals the shocking details of beatings, imprisonment and 'honour' killings, the women driven to suicide and also hears from those on the run, in fear of their lives.

videos.title: Murdoch's TV Pirates
videos.overview: As Rupert Murdoch faces accusations of law-breaking at his British tabloids, Panorama reveals fresh hacking allegations striking at the heart of News Corporation's pay-TV empire.

videos.title: The Honeymoon Murder
videos.overview: With exclusive access to publicly unseen CCTV footage, this Panorama special examines in detail the hours leading up to the death of Anni Dewani while on honeymoon in Cape Town.

videos.title: The Great Apprentice Scandal
videos.overview: Panorama's Shelley Jofre investigates problems reported in government supported apprenticeship schemes, a flagship programme for getting young unemployed people in to work.

videos.title: Ivory Wars: Out of Africa
videos.overview: Rageh Omaar goes on the trail of ivory poachers, smugglers and organised crime syndicates to investigate the plight of Africa's elephants.

videos.title: Billionaires Behaving Badly?
videos.overview: Current affairs. Glencore is a commodity giant that trades huge quantities of wheat, coal and much of the world's copper. John Sweeney talks to its boss, Ivan Glasenberg.

videos.title: Undercover: Elderly Care
videos.overview: Current affairs. Panorama reveals the appalling treatment of an elderly care home resident with dementia, captured on film after a concerned relative hid a secret camera.

videos.title: Madeleine: The Last Hope?
videos.overview: Current affairs. The senior UK investigator in the Madeleine McCann case speaks about why he believes he has the best opportunity yet to solve the mystery of her disappearance.

videos.title: The Truth About Tax
videos.overview: Panorama investigates how some of the UK's most famous companies have been using a tax haven at the heart of Europe to save millions in tax.

videos.title: Eurovision's Dirty Secret
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover inside Eurovision host nation Azerbaijan to reveal the truth about this secretive country and its approach to the world's most watched non-sporting event.

videos.title: Euro 2012: Stadiums of Hate
videos.overview: With days to go before the kick-off of the Euro 2012 championships, Panorama reveals evidence of racist violence and anti-semitism at the heart of Polish and Ukrainian football.

videos.title: Life and Debt: A Greek Tragedy
videos.overview: John Humphrys investigates the economic crisis in Greece, meeting ordinary Greeks and exploring how the outcome of the upcoming election may signpost the future of Europe.

videos.title: Call Centres Undercover
videos.overview: Britain is being affected by an 'epidemic' of unsolicited and unwanted calls and texts. With an estimated three billion marketing calls and messages received every year, Panorama goes undercover to expose how some firms are getting round the regulations designed to protect consumers.

videos.title: Britain on the Brink: Back to the 70s?
videos.overview: Britain is suffering the longest peacetime slump in decades. Panorama asks whether Britain is able to cope with a new age of austerity with surprising echoes of the 1970s.

videos.title: Britain's Biggest Waste Dumpers
videos.overview: Raphael Rowe tracks down some of Britain's biggest illegal fly-tippers, criminals who have pocketed tens of thousands of pounds handed over by motorists to recycle used tyres.

videos.title: The Truth About Sports Products
videos.overview: Panorama investigates sports products that promise to boost your performance. Shelley Jofre tests the science behind the advertising claims made by some of sport's biggest brands.

videos.title: Disabled or Faking It?
videos.overview: Declan Lawn reports on plans to get millions of people claiming disability benefits back into work. But will new assessment tests victimise those who deserve the most support?

videos.title: Rats, Traps, Bugs and Cutbacks
videos.overview: Budget cuts mean some councils are disbanding pest control teams and others are charging for previously free services. Will this lead to more pests and the diseases they carry?

videos.title: Justice Denied: The Greatest Scandal?
videos.overview: Twenty years after a Panorama investigation helped to clear the Cardiff Three, the same team returns to investigate why the trial against the police officers collapsed last year.

videos.title: Kony: Hunt for the World's Most Wanted
videos.overview: Reporter Sorious Samura investigates the myths surrounding one of Africa's most bizarre and brutal criminals, Joseph Kony, and the international fight to bring him to justice.

videos.title: Dial 999... and Wait?
videos.overview: With police, fire and ambulance services facing cuts in public spending, Panorama examines the effect on 999 response times. Declan Lawn reveals the areas where people needing immediate help from our emergency services are left waiting, and investigates claims that lives are being put at risk.

videos.title: Old, Drunk and Disorderly?
videos.overview: Joan Bakewell investigates alcohol problems among those aged 65 and over, the age group most likely to drink every day, at home and alone.

videos.title: Trouble on the Estate
videos.overview: Panorama visits a housing estate in Blackburn, learning what it is like to live there. The programme follows families, children and police, and goes undercover with drug dealers.

videos.title: Price Tag Wars
videos.overview: Panorama presents an insight into the world of the so-called Price Taggers, a group of Israeli teenagers who believe every Palestinian attack should be met with an act of revenge.

videos.title: Reading, Writing and Rip-Offs
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the computer supply companies whose directors have grown rich signing up hundreds of schools to deals that have taken them to the brink of bankruptcy.

videos.title: Undercover: Debt on the Doorstep
videos.overview: With the economy showing few signs of recovery, reporter Richard Bilton investigates the thriving debt business - a world of cash on the doorstep and high interest rates.

videos.title: Britain's Secret Health Tourists
videos.overview: Declan Lawn reports on how 'health tourists' are obtaining free NHS treatment they should be paying for, at a cost of millions to the health service.

videos.title: Return of the Supergrass
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the deals being offered to often violent gangsters to become the next generation of supergrasses in an effort to tackle violent crime.

videos.title: Kill at Will? America on Trial
videos.overview: Ahead of America's costliest-ever elections, Raphael Rowe investigates how lobby groups helped create laws blamed for one of the most controversial killings in recent US history.

videos.title: Jimmy Savile - What the BBC Knew
videos.overview: A Panorama Special investigates the Jimmy Savile child abuse scandal and asks what the BBC knew in the past, and examines the events around the dropping of the Corporation's own Newsnight investigation into the subject.

videos.title: The Hospital That Stopped Caring
videos.overview: A year after Panorama exposed the violent abuse patients suffered at the Winterbourne View hospital, Alison Holt investigates if society's most vulnerable are any better protected.

videos.title: Gambling Nation
videos.overview: With casino-style gambling now available day or night at the touch of a button in our homes and on our phones, Panorama explores its popularity... and reveals a darker side.

videos.title: Badgers: Dodging the Bullet?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the government's sudden decision last month to postpone its controversial badger cull, days before it was due to start. Will the cull be enforced next year?

videos.title: The Mind Reader: Unlocking My Voice
videos.overview: Panorama follows a group of severely brain injured patients and reveals the revolutionary efforts made to help them communicate with their families and the outside world.

videos.title: Who's Watching the Detectives?
videos.overview: Mark Daly investigates whether the Independent Police Complaints Commission is fit for purpose, and if it has sufficient power or independence to hold the police to account.

videos.title: Undercover: How to Dodge Tax
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover to investigate corporate service providers - the people and companies who sell corporate anonymity and access to offshore tax havens.

videos.title: How Safe is Your Hospital?
videos.overview: With the NHS under huge pressure, Panorama reveals poor patient care is putting thousands of people at risk of death or serious injury every year.

videos.title: The Secret Drone War
videos.overview: Panorama goes to Waziristan to report on the drone war and to find out from its victims why they are seeking justice in the British courts.

videos.title: Britain's Hidden Housing Crisis
videos.overview: Panorama Special that follows four stories over five months and reveals the devastating impact of being evicted from your own home and losing everything.

videos.title: The Tax Haven Twins
videos.overview: Reporter John Sweeney investigates the secretive world of the billionaire Barclay twins. Sir Frederick and Sir David Barclay own the paper that exposed the MPs' expenses scandal. So why do they hate it when the spotlight is turned on them?

videos.title: Immigration Undercover
videos.overview: Reporter Paul Kenyon goes undercover with the new type of gang smuggling illegal immigrants out of the UK as well as in, right under the nose of the British authorities.

videos.title: The Great Disability Scam?
videos.overview: Only half of people with a disability are in work. Panorama investigates if one of the government's most ambitious welfare reforms can solve the problem of disability unemployment.

videos.title: The Great Abortion Divide
videos.overview: Victoria Derbyshire investigates the great abortion divide between Northern Ireland and most of the United Kingdom, and asks if it is time to change the law.

videos.title: Inside Barclays: Banking on Bonuses
videos.overview: After a series of controversies, bosses at Barclays say they're changing the culture of the bank. But what went wrong? Reporter Richard Bilton investigates the bonus culture that drove one of our biggest banks.

videos.title: What's Really in our Food?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the horse meat scandal and reveals more concerns about what is really in our food. Richard Bilton questions the 'light touch' regulation of the food industry.

videos.title: Mission Accomplished? Secrets of Helmand
videos.overview: Reporter Ben Anderson joins Allied troops preparing to hand over to Afghan forces next year, finding the Afghan army and police to be poorly trained and lacking resources.

videos.title: America's Gun Addiction
videos.overview: Following the Newtown massacre, Panorama meets the teachers who want to use guns to protect their schools and reveals America's national crisis in mental healthcare.

videos.title: The Spies Who Fooled the World
videos.overview: On the eve of the tenth anniversary of the Iraq War, Panorama reveals how key aspects of the secret intelligence used to justify the invasion were based on fabrication and lies.

videos.title: The Derby Fire: Secrets and Lies
videos.overview: The Derby fire, in which six children died, was an attack on a family that shocked the country. Panorama asks were warnings missed?

videos.title: North Korea Undercover
videos.overview: Panorama reporter John Sweeney spends eight days undercover inside North Korea, the most rigidly-controlled nation on Earth.

videos.title: Secrets of Britain's Sharia Councils
videos.overview: Panorama reporter Jane Corbin goes undercover to investigate what is really happening in Britain's Sharia Councils - Islamic religious courts.

videos.title: The Russians Are Coming
videos.overview: Reporter Darragh MacIntyre investigates a death in a Russian prison that has brought the threat of violence to the UK, and the death of a whistleblower found in Surrey.

videos.title: Jobs for the Boys?
videos.overview: Former England and Arsenal footballer Sol Campbell investigates why the unemployment rate for young black British men is roughly double that of their white counterparts.

videos.title: Hillsborough - How They Buried the Truth
videos.overview: A Panorama investigation reveals how police, politicians, lawyers and judges all played a part in burying the truth about Britain's worst football disaster.

videos.title: Cancer: Hope for Sale?
videos.overview: Richard Bilton investigates a controversial American doctor who claims he can cure cancer. Why has he been allowed to sell an unproven and experimental treatment for 30 years?

videos.title: Cash for Questions Undercover
videos.overview: A Panorama special going undercover to reveal lobbying practices which raise serious questions about standards in political life.

videos.title: Blacklist Britain
videos.overview: Richard Bilton does the first TV interview with the bookkeeper for the organisation which ran a secret blacklist subscribed to by some of the biggest names in British business.

videos.title: Traffic Fines - Highway Robbery?
videos.overview: With councils fining drivers in ever-greater numbers after capturing them on CCTV, Panorama tries to find new ways to cut down on the mountain of traffic tickets issued each year.

videos.title: Elderly Care: Condition Critical?
videos.overview: Using secret filming and exclusive research into the mortality rates of care and nursing homes for the elderly in England, Panorama exposes the pain of poor care and neglect.

videos.title: Kids Lost in Care
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the standard of residential care for vulnerable children. In homes where care is not up to scratch, some young people run away into risky situations.

videos.title: The Truth about Pills and Pregnancy
videos.overview: Current affairs. Many women have to take medicines while pregnant. But could they be risking the health of their unborn child? Reporter Shelley Jofre investigates.

videos.title: The Trouble with Trump
videos.overview: Current affairs. Reporter John Sweeney asks if the Scottish government knew enough about self-proclaimed billionaire Donald Trump before accepting his investment proposal.

videos.title: Broken by Battle
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the true personal cost of the war in Afghanistan on British troops, going beyond the limits of the Ministry of Defence's statistics on suicide.

videos.title: Jungle Outlaws: The Chainsaw Trail
videos.overview: Panorama investigates illegal logging in the rainforest and the timber trail from Africa to West Europe. Raphael Rowe spent six months tracking logs from Congo's jungle.

videos.title: Tainted Love: Secrets of the Dating Game
videos.overview: Legal notice - this episode is the subject of a legal complaint. Reporter Fiona Walker investigates how unscrupulous dating websites are preying on those looking for love.

videos.title: The Brothers Who Bombed Boston
videos.overview: Panorama explores how the two suspected Boston Marathon bombers - brothers raised and educated in the US - became radicalised, and asks if America's war on terror has come home.

videos.title: Locked Up For Being Ill?
videos.overview: Current affairs. With police estimating that dealing with mental health patients takes up 25 percent of their time, Paul Kenyon discovers a world of self-harm and suicide attempts.

videos.title: Tax, Lies and Videotape
videos.overview: Current affairs. Panorama goes undercover in the City to investigate the truth about UK tax policy, discovering how London is still home to the tax avoidance industry.

videos.title: The Honeymoon Murder: Who Killed Anni?
videos.overview: With access to secret police files, Jeremy Vine looks at the case against the Bristol businessman accused of killing his young bride on honeymoon in South Africa in 2010.

videos.title: Dying for a Bargain
videos.overview: Panorama investigates how our clothes - including those of some big high street brands - are really made, finding evidence of an industry that still puts profit before safety.

videos.title: Terror in Nairobi
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the network al-Shabab uses to cross the Somali-Kenyan border at will and this terror group's appeal to radicalised Muslim youths in Britain and beyond.

videos.title: Saving Syria's Children
videos.overview: In a special edition, Panorama travels with British doctors inside Syria to exclusively reveal the devastating impact of the war on children caught in the conflict.

videos.title: Malala: Shot for Going to School
videos.overview: One year ago, Malala Yousafzai was shot by the Taliban on her school bus. In this Panorama special, she talks exclusively to Mishal Husain about her remarkable journey.

videos.title: Britain's New Banking Scandal
videos.overview: Panorama reporter Adam Shaw lifts the lid on what could be Britain's biggest financial mis-selling scandal - the hard sell of so-called interest rate swaps.

videos.title: Murder in the Alps
videos.overview: With exclusive access to eyewitnesses and investigators, Panorama reveals how and asks why a British family and a French cyclist were brutally murdered by a hitman.

videos.title: Our Dirty Nation
videos.overview: Cleaning up Britain's rubbish costs more than a billion pounds each year. Journalist and Labour peer Joan Bakewell argues that we all need to take more pride in our surroundings.

videos.title: After Savile: No More Secrets?
videos.overview: In Britain, turning a blind eye to child abuse in a school, hospital or a church is not a crime; Panorama talks to victims, police and senior figures calling for the law to change.

videos.title: The Great House Price Bubble?
videos.overview: With house prices hitting record highs at the same time as living standards continue to be squeezed, Adam Shaw goes in search of affordable homes for ordinary working families.

videos.title: Britain's Secret Terror Force
videos.overview: Reporter John Ware interviews former members of a secret undercover unit run by the British Army in the early 1970s as they reveal how they took the war to the IRA.

videos.title: Amazon: The Truth Behind the Click
videos.overview: How well does online retailer Amazon treat its workers? Conditions in the company's giant warehouses have been condemned by unions as among the worst in Britain.

videos.title: Where's Our Aid Money Gone?
videos.overview: Current affairs. With the Global Fund's inspector general sacked for 'unsatisfactory' performance after exposing corruption, Richard Bilton challenges those responsible.

videos.title: Energy Bills: Power Failure?
videos.overview: Current affairs. Energy bills have gone up by around a quarter in the past four years and politicians from all sides say they are determined to bring them down. Can they deliver?

videos.title: All in a Good Cause
videos.overview: Current affairs. Do we really know about the charities we support? Declan Lawn hears from donors and charity workers who believe the quest for money is undermining the mission.

videos.title: The Romanians are Coming?
videos.overview: Reporter Paul Kenyon joins British police in a Romanian village where most of the men have left to pursue work in the black markets of London, as they try to stem the flow.

videos.title: Woolwich: The Untold Story
videos.overview: With two British Muslim converts found guilty of the murder of Drummer Lee Rigby, Panorama asks if the security services among others missed opportunities to prevent Lee's death.

videos.title: I Want My Baby Back
videos.overview: Panorama reporter John Sweeney investigates the secretive world of the family courts and asks whether some parents may have unfairly lost their children forever.

videos.title: Police: Shooting to Kill?
videos.overview: Reporter Alistair Jackson investigates the tactics of the country's police firearms units, and officers who have killed break their silence to speak out to Panorama.

videos.title: Putin's Games
videos.overview: Panorama investigates claims that lucrative contracts for the Winter Olympics have been handed to President Putin's friends, and that billions have been embezzled by fraudsters.

videos.title: Educating North Korea
videos.overview: Reporter Chris Rogers travels to North Korea, where a university paid for by the west is attempting to open the minds of the secretive state's future elite.

videos.title: Immigration Undercover: The Student Visa Scandal
videos.overview: Reporter Richard Watson goes undercover to expose Britain's multimillion-pound trade in immigration visas and the frauds that allow bogus foreign students to remain in the UK.

videos.title: Britain Underwater
videos.overview: As Britain is battered yet again by extreme weather, reporter Richard Bilton investigates the causes of the flooding that has devastated so much of the country.

videos.title: Kidnapped: Betrayed by Britain?
videos.overview: Panorama investigates the disappearance in Dubai of a British businessman, as the UK government stands accused of ignoring warnings that their actions posed a risk to his life.

videos.title: Hungry Britain?
videos.overview: With hundreds of thousands of people across the country now getting free handouts of food, reporter Darragh MacIntyre investigates the dramatic rise in the number of food banks.

videos.title: The Revolution that Shook the World
videos.overview: As Russia and the West square up to each other over Ukraine, Paul Kenyon reports from inside the flashpoint military bases of Crimea as they are surrounded by Russian troops.

videos.title: A Week in A&E: Condition Critical?
videos.overview: Vivian White spends a week in a hospital in Stockton, hearing from doctors and nurses about the relentless pressure of working to strict government waiting time targets.

videos.title: The Great NHS Robbery
videos.overview: Panorama investigates fraud in the National Health Service. With the NHS under financial pressure, Fiona Walker hears claims that it is losing billions each year to fraudsters.

videos.title: The Mayor and Our Money
videos.overview: John Ware reports on the system of directly-elected mayors, focussing on Tower Hamlets in London. Has it led to too much power being concentrated into the hands of one politician?

videos.title: The Pope's Revolution
videos.overview: On the eve of the Queen's historic trip to the Vatican, Jane Corbin examines Pope Francis' shake-up of the Catholic Church. Are his reforms more about style than substance?

videos.title: Don't Take My Car: Bailiffs Undercover
videos.overview: Panorama goes undercover to expose the bailiffs who seize cars and demand huge fees in what has become a multimillion-pound business: chasing unpaid parking tickets.

videos.title: Don't Cap My Benefits
videos.overview: As the government's benefits changes begin to bite, Panorama gains exclusive access to one of London's worst-hit boroughs and follows the personal stories of those most affected.

videos.title: Who's Paying Your Doctor?
videos.overview: With the NHS drug bill topping £10 billion in 2013, this investigation examines the tactics employed by drug companies to tap into that lucrative market.

videos.title: Bernie Ecclestone: Lies, Bribes and Formula One
videos.overview: Panorama's Darragh Macintyre investigates the truth about F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone, and asks why he is still in charge after two courts say he paid a 44 million dollar bribe.

videos.title: Behind Closed Doors: Elderly Care Exposed
videos.overview: Panorama investigates what life can be like inside the world of elderly care with the aid of undercover filming, and asks if parts of the system are letting down a generation.

videos.title: From Jail to Jihad?
videos.overview: The current affairs programme investigates the radicalisation of some Muslims within the prison system, as Raphael Rowe interviews extremists about their experiences inside.

videos.title: Behind the Balaclavas
videos.overview: Paul Kenyon follows the men who have become some of the most powerful in the Ukraine conflict, including a former history teacher and a former businessman who now leads an army.

videos.title: Savile: The Power to Abuse
videos.overview: Shelley Jofre investigates why Jimmy Savile was given access to vulnerable patients at Broadmoor Hospital and asks how the DJ got so close to the heart of Britain's establishment.

videos.title: Brazil: In the Shadow of the Stadiums
videos.overview: Brazil is hosting the 2014 World Cup, but the build-up has been overshadowed by violent protests against the spiralling cost of staging the tournament.

videos.title: Undercover: Justice for Sale?
videos.overview: An investigation by Panorama discovers experts in handwriting, CCTV analysis and animal behaviour prepared to help clients hide the truth in breach of professional obligations.

videos.title: Britain's Homeless Families
videos.overview: Richard Bilton meets families forced out by private landlords and asks whether the government's increasing reliance on the private rental sector is placing the vulnerable at risk.

videos.title: Hacking: Power, Corruption and Lies
videos.overview: Panorama Special in which Robert Peston investigates the questions behind the phone hacking trial which saw David Cameron's former spokesman, Andy Coulson, convicted.

videos.title: Bedlam Behind Bars
videos.overview: With access to two US jails, reporter Hilary Andersson finds that American prisons are having to accommodate vast numbers of inmates with serious mental health problems.

videos.title: Isis: Terror in Iraq
videos.overview: An investigation into Isis and how it is ripping Iraq apart. Paul Wood speaks to members of the terror group and sees the fighting in Iraq first-hand. Will British recruits bring the terror home?

videos.title: Drivers Who Kill
videos.overview: Every day five people die on Britain's roads - but they seldom make headlines. Is this complacency leading to a lack of justice for victims and their families?

videos.title: Last Chance Academy
videos.overview: The story of one school's groundbreaking battle to save problem pupils from the scrap heap and bring exam success.

videos.title: Stolen Childhoods: The Grooming Scandal
videos.overview: Alison Holt investigates the grooming and sexual exploitation of children which has devastated lives in the South Yorkshire town of Rotherham for more than twenty years.

videos.title: Putin's Gamble
videos.overview: Vladimir Putin stands accused of launching an undeclared war against Ukraine. As fears of a wider war grow, John Sweeney challenges the Russian strongman on the killing in Ukraine.

videos.title: Scotland's Decision
videos.overview: In the week Scotland goes to the ballot box, reporter Allan Little explores what has happened in the past four decades to transform the question of Scottish independence and how it has come to dominate British politics.

videos.title: Scotland: The People's Voice
videos.overview: In the aftermath of Scotland's referendum, Panorama follows the lives of ordinary voters who took part in the momentous decision.

videos.title: The War of the Tunnels
videos.overview: Jane Corbin investigates the conflict involving Israel and Gaza and goes deep into the tunnels where battles have been fought.

videos.title: Born Asleep
videos.overview: Every year in the UK, over 3,000 babies are stillborn. Panorama's Paul Kenyon meets the clinicians who say they could save hundreds of babies' lives a year.

videos.title: Workers on the Breadline
